D006 still contains it, so Claude can read it there", and D006 is marked "Available". People.dc.html shows D006 with "'Annie' not yet replaced". Unlock repeats "Claude only ever works with the de-identified copy."
findings.recommendation: Build the PD-AI 4.11 answer from what actually happened. If any published document contained an identifier Claude could read, say so (for example "one nickname was exposed in D006 between X and Y"). Use hedged wording such as 'names and identifiers we detected were replaced'. A statement to the Court that may be untrue goes against PD-AI 4.4 (the duty not to mislead).

findings.title: Choosing a commercial plan is treated as meeting all of PD-AI 5.5
findings.evidence: Settings says: "Team, Enterprise or API (commercial) — No training on your data under the commercial terms. Restricted documents are shared, de-identified." The intro text reduces 5.5 to "enforceable confidentiality terms that doesn't train on it". Documents says: "Restricted material is withheld from consumer Claude plans (PD-AI 5.5)."
findings.recommendation: PD-AI 5.5 has three parts: (1) the information stays in a closed environment that unauthorised third parties can't reach, under enforceable confidentiality restrictions on the supplier; (2) it is not used for training; (3) it is used only in connection with the proceeding to which it relates. The user must also be satisfied of these, and 5.5 itself warns that such assurances are often unavailable. Ask the user to confirm each part and say they have read the terms (PD-AI 4.18), log that confirmation, and still release restricted documents one at a time rather than automatically. Avoid wording that implies the product makes the use compliant.

findings.title: The 'Ordinary' default misses much material that PD-AI 5.5 restricts
findings.evidence: The import options are "Ordinary / Discovery / disclosure / Subpoenaed / Under suppression order", and "Ordinary" is the default. The Document details select has only "Ordinary" and "Subpoenaed".
findings.recommendation: PD-AI 5.5 also covers documents produced under a court order for production and anything under a statutory, court-ordered or implied restriction on use. In parenting matters that usually takes in the other party's disclosure (implied undertaking), family reports and Child Impact Reports, Notices of Risk, and material produced by child-protection or police agencies. Ask 'How did you get this document?' at import (yours / from the other party / from the court or a court-ordered report / under subpoena / other), and warn when the answer points to a restricted category. Use the same category list in Document.dc.html.

findings.title: Subpoena handling ignores the access terms that come with produced material
findings.evidence: D009 "Subpoenaed school attendance records" is imported as text and marked "Withheld · subpoena". Nothing records whether the party was allowed to copy it or only to inspect it, or any order limiting its use.
findings.recommendation: In the FCFCOA, access to subpoenaed material can be limited, for example to inspection only for sensitive records. If so, the user may not be entitled to hold a copy in any app. Record the access terms and any relevant orders for each subpoenaed document. Warn before importing inspect-only material, and keep a use-only-in-this-proceeding note in the log. A lawyer should confirm the exact rule references.

findings.title: Withheld material can still reach Claude indirectly
findings.evidence: The issue "Children's schooling and attendance" shows "3 supporting · withheld source". The document title "Subpoenaed school attendance records" describes what it contains. The Draft invites "Add a paragraph in your own words (real names are fine)", and Claude reads drafts and notes in tokenised form.
findings.recommendation: Assume titles, issue text, chronology entries and draft paragraphs can carry the content of subpoenaed or discovered material. Hide or neutralise titles of withheld documents in Claude's view. Flag or keep from Claude any user-written text that cites a withheld document. Tell the user plainly that retelling restricted content in a draft still counts as entering it into an AI tool.

findings.title: Claude's draft paragraph adds a state of mind that no source supports
findings.evidence: Paragraph 4 (Claude's text) says "...because I was worried about how upset Mia gets when nobody comes." The only cited source, D001:3, says only "this is the third time this term." Unlike chronology entries, draft paragraphs show no source citations.
findings.recommendation: Show the source lines behind each Claude-drafted paragraph, and highlight any clause (especially feelings, motives or opinions) that no cited line supports. An invented state of mind in sworn evidence is exactly the content PD-AI 4.4–4.6 and 4.9 warn about.

findings.title: The affidavit draft lacks the required court form
findings.evidence: The Draft is six bare numbered paragraphs plus "Export with real names". There is no court heading or file number, no applicant/respondent names, and no deponent details. There is no choice between swearing and affirming, no jurat or witness block, and no page signature lines. Paragraph 1 says "from my own knowledge", but nothing handles statements of information and belief or their sources.
findings.recommendation: Export to the FCFCOA affidavit layout: court and file number, parties and their roles, deponent's name, occupation and address (with an option to withhold an address where there are safety concerns), oath or affirmation, and signature and witness blocks. Prompt for the source of any belief or hearsay. Check the length rules for interim affidavits, since PD-AI 4.6 expects compliance with length limits.

findings.title: No annexure workflow, and text transcripts aren't the original evidence
findings.evidence: Text messages (D001) exist only as imported .txt lines ("14/03/2025 3:05pm Anna: ..."). The Draft has no way to attach a document as an annexure, and nothing keeps the original screenshots, PDFs or emails.
findings.recommendation: Let the user mark documents as annexures to an affidavit, with marks (for example "Annexure AT-1"), a cover sheet for the witness's certification, and paragraph text referring to the annexure. Annex the original file (screenshots showing sender and date), never the tokenised or retyped text. Store or link originals in the vault. PD-AI 4.6 requires authenticity, and a retyped exchange is easy to attack.

findings.title: Citations like D002:9 mean nothing to the Court
findings.evidence: Chronology sources read "D002:9 · D001:1–2". In D002, line 9 is affidavit paragraph 4. Chronology has an "Export" button with no format shown.
findings.recommendation: Keep line references for checking inside the app. On export, convert them to references the Court uses: "Affidavit of A Thornbury sworn 2 April 2025 at [4]", "Annexure AT-2", subpoena material by producing party and tab. Track whether each document is filed, served or relied on, and on what date. Export chronologies as a date / event / source table suitable for a case outline.

findings.title: No support for the Notice of Risk and other procedural documents
findings.evidence: Drafts offers only "Affidavit", "Case outline" and "Letter to the other side". People roles are family roles only (mother, father, maternal_grandmother, class_teacher). There are no party roles (Applicant/Respondent), no Independent Children's Lawyer and no family consultant. There is nowhere to record existing orders or a parenting plan.
findings.recommendation: Add document types for the Notice of Child Abuse, Family Violence or Risk (required in parenting proceedings and expected to match the affidavit), the s 60I certificate and genuine steps, and current orders. Then late collections can be checked against what the orders actually require. Add party and professional roles that match FCFCOA terminology. Tie the 'Case outline' draft to whatever outline format the Court has directed. The exact form requirements are not shown in the files.

findings.title: Nothing about filing through the Commonwealth Courts Portal
findings.evidence: Export says only "Exports download to your computer, never into the case folder." Nothing covers output format, signing and witnessing before filing, combining annexures, or service.
findings.recommendation: Export a PDF suitable for filing (affidavit plus annexures in order, page numbers). Add a short pre-filing checklist: print, sign every page, swear or affirm before an authorised witness, scan, file on the Portal, serve the other party (and the ICL if one is appointed). Point the user to the Court's own guidance rather than restating filing rules that may change.

findings.title: PD-AI 5.4 (turn off web search and chat history) isn't covered for Claude Code
findings.evidence: Settings mentions only "Turn off 'Help improve Claude'" and lists "Claude Code sandbox for this folder: on". Nothing covers Claude Code's web search and web fetch tools, or locally stored conversation history. The product can't confirm the training opt-out either.
findings.recommendation: Configure or check that web search and web fetch are disabled for the case folder, and explain where Claude Code keeps conversation history. Record in the Log the settings the user confirmed, including the training opt-out, so the 4.11 answer can cover PD-AI 5.4.

findings.title: The 4.11 summary leaves out the local AI models and one of the four questions
findings.evidence: "Which tool?" names only "Claude (Claude Code, Pro plan)". Elsewhere the product runs an on-device name model and optionally a local language model on the original documents. The summary answers whether AI was used, which tool, how it was checked and confidentiality. It doesn't cover the fourth question in 4.11, 'how the principles in this Practice Direction have been observed', such as own-words affidavits and checks of legal references.
findings.recommendation: PD-AI 1.6 applies the obligations whether or not a product is labelled as AI, so list every AI component used. Add a line on own words in affidavits (Claude-originated paragraphs counted honestly) and on checking any law Claude cited.

findings.title: Removing names doesn't make the content safe to share
findings.evidence: Copy throughout implies tokenisation is enough protection ("Claude only ever works with the de-identified copy"). Yet the content Claude reads still includes children's illnesses, school-attendance patterns and family conflict, which are the 'medical records' and safety-sensitive details named in PD-AI 3.3 (Safety). A consumer plan sits near the PD's definition of 'Public AI' in 5.4.
findings.recommendation: Say plainly that removing names lowers the risk but doesn't remove it. Unusual facts can identify a family (Part XIVB), and some content (medical, family-violence, protected-address context) may need to be withheld even after tokenising. Offer a 'sensitive content' flag besides the restricted-source categories.

findings.title: Claude's suggestions edge toward legal advice without a caveat
findings.evidence: "Claude suggests: say what time, and why it suits the children." The issue is "raised by Claude". Nothing reminds the user that PD-AI 4.17 makes legal advice and the assessment of strengths and weaknesses the role of a lawyer. Nothing points to free legal help.
findings.recommendation: Add a short, persistent note on the Issues and Drafts screens that Claude isn't a lawyer, with links to Legal Aid, family law advice lines or duty lawyer services. Frame suggestions around the questions the Court considers (the child's best interests) rather than tactics.

findings.title: Strength: verification is built into the workflow and tied to the PD
findings.evidence: Chronology shows the source lines next to each Claude entry and notices a real discrepancy ("the messages only mention Mia"). "Verifying records that you checked it (PD-AI 4.7). If it changes later, it goes back to 'to check'." Paste flags an unknown token ("Claude may have invented a person") and prompts AustLII checks (PD-AI 4.6–4.7). Issues includes evidence against the user's case, not only for it.
findings.recommendation: Keep this. Extend the same source-beside-claim pattern to affidavit drafts (see the finding on unsupported statements in paragraph 4).

findings.title: Strength: refuses the local model that would send text off the computer
findings.evidence: "Not used: text would leave this computer — 'deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud' is an Ollama cloud model. Ollama forwards requests to ollama.com, even though the address is local." Detection status shows "Language model: refused".
findings.recommendation: Keep this. It reflects a real understanding of PD-AI 4.18–4.19 and 5.1, which is rare. Log the refusal so it can be included in the 4.11 answer.

lens: A judicial officer or registrar receiving documents prepared with this product: what would you want to see, what would worry you (accuracy, AI-written content presented as evidence, citations, disclosure of AI use under PD-AI 4.11, safety of children's information)? Does the product help the litigant meet PD-AI 4.4-4.11 and 5.x in substance, not just in form? Check against PD-AI.txt.
summary: From the bench, casefile does more on PD-AI compliance than most tools would. Affidavit export is blocked until every Claude paragraph is rewritten or adopted. Adopting a paragraph needs two attestations. Chronology checking puts the source lines side by side with the entry and flags where they disagree. Tokens Claude may have made up are caught. The log is tamper-evident and comes with a ready 4.11 summary. But several mechanisms meet the PD in form more than in substance. A light edit turns Claude's wording into "your words" at a 50% similarity line. Text pasted from outside the tracked flow has no record of where it came from. Only affidavits get authorship tracking; chronologies and other drafts can be exported unchecked. Nothing checks legal citations, even though PD 4.7 singles them out. The restricted-material model covers only discovery, subpoena and suppression. It leaves out family reports, medical and counselling records, protected addresses and material under an implied undertaking, which PD 3.3 and 5.5 also cover. Fix those and a registrar could trust both what is filed and the litigant's answer if asked how AI was used.

findings.title: A 50% similarity line re-labels Claude's drafting as the witness's own words
findings.evidence: Paragraph 4 is "Claude wrote this · editing". A meter with a midpoint mark reads "38% · will count as your words". The Log's 4.11 summary counts paragraphs as "1 affidavit paragraph adopted, 3 written by me". Once para 4 drops below the line it would presumably be counted as "written by me", though Claude drafted it and the user reworded it.
findings.recommendation: Keep where a paragraph came from as a permanent attribute, separate from how similar it now is. Record "drafted by Claude, rewritten by you" and say so in the log and the 4.11 summary. Do not let a word-overlap metric decide what PD 4.9 means by "the witness's own words". Use the similarity figure only as a hint, and still require the adopt-style attestation for any paragraph that started as Claude's.

findings.title: No way to check citations to case law or legislation
findings.evidence: The only nod to PD 4.7's citation duty is footer text on Paste: "Check facts, dates and any law Claude mentions on AustLII before relying on them (PD-AI 4.6–4.7)". Drafts lists a "Case outline · 14 paragraphs" and a "Letter to the other side" that could contain legal propositions. Unlike D-line citations, nothing detects, lists or tracks the verification of case or legislation references.
findings.recommendation: Detect references to authorities and legislation in anything Claude writes. Show each one as an unverified item with a link to AustLII or the Federal Register of Legislation. Ask the user to confirm the authority exists, says what it is cited for, is current, and that any quotes are exact. Block export until that is done, as already happens for Claude's affidavit paragraphs. Flag non-Australian authorities.

findings.title: Restricted categories leave out sensitive family-law material the PD names
findings.evidence: The import options are "Ordinary / Discovery / disclosure / Subpoenaed / Under suppression order". The Document detail's Kind select offers only "Ordinary" and "Subpoenaed". PD 5.5 also covers material "subject to a statutory, court ordered or implied prohibition", such as the other party's served affidavits and family reports. PD 3.3 (Safety) names protected residential addresses and medical records. The Issues list has a "Medical care" issue, and D001:7 (a child's temperature) goes to Claude as an ordinary document.
findings.recommendation: Add categories for: court-produced reports (family reports, s 11F/ICL material); notices of risk; medical, counselling and therapy records; material under a protected address or confidentiality order; and other parties' documents held under the implied undertaking. Default these to withheld on a consumer plan, or to tokenised-and-reviewed with a safety warning. Make the Kind control on the Document screen match the import options.

findings.title: Text pasted from outside the tracked flow can enter the affidavit as the user's own words
findings.evidence: Paste "See anything Claude wrote with the real names back in ... nothing is sent anywhere" has a Copy button for the de-tokenised text. Draft offers "Add a paragraph in your own words (real names are fine)". Nothing shows that a pasted or copied paragraph keeps a Claude label, or that Paste use is logged.
findings.recommendation: Record each Paste conversion in the AI-use log. When text added to a draft closely matches recent Claude output (from Paste, notes or the CLI), tag it as Claude's wording and send it through the adopt or rewrite gate. At minimum, warn on Paste's Copy that Claude's text must not be added to an affidavit as the user's own words.

findings.title: Chronology and non-affidavit drafts can be exported with unchecked Claude content
findings.evidence: The Chronology has an always-enabled "Export" button while it shows "To check 5". One entry reads "Grandmother {{grandmother}} starts Wednesday pickups ... can't verify" with no source citation. In Drafts, only the affidavit shows authorship counts ("2 need you"). "Case outline · 14 paragraphs" and "Letter to the other side · 5 paragraphs" show no tracking.
findings.recommendation: Apply the same rule to every exported document. Either block export while Claude content is unchecked, or export it visibly marked "unverified" and leave it out of filing-ready output. Do not allow uncited Claude chronology entries at all. Show authorship tracking for outlines and letters, since PD 4.4 extends the duty not to mislead to the other parties too.

findings.title: "Verified" means the source says it, not that it is true or independent
findings.evidence: The Chronology checker asks "Does the source say this?", and the 2025-03-14 entry rests on D002:9, the user's own affidavit. In Issues, D001:3 ("Anna: Mr Okafor, this is the third time this term.") is listed under Supports with Claude's note "Shows a pattern — third late collection this term", and D002:9 is labelled "Your sworn account". The mother's own assertions are presented as proof of a pattern, and Claude's own note says the other two late collections "aren't in any document".
findings.recommendation: Rename the state to something like "checked against source". Mark entries whose only source is the user's own statement or affidavit. Make the user check Claude's characterisation ("shows a pattern") separately from the quoted line. The 4.11 summary's "verified against the source lines" is accurate wording; keep the UI's wording just as precise.

findings.title: The 4.11 summary claims protections the app cannot check, and skips PD 5.4
findings.evidence: Settings, for a consumer plan, says only "Turn off 'Help improve Claude' in Claude's privacy settings". PD 5.4 also requires disabling chat history and web search where available. Nothing covers Claude Code's web or fetch tools. The plan choice is self-declared ("Team, Enterprise or API (commercial) ... Restricted documents are shared"). Under "How was confidential material protected?" the Log summary says nothing about training or history settings.
findings.recommendation: Add a PD 5.4 checklist: training off, chat history and retention settings, and web search and fetch disabled for this folder (configured through the Claude Code sandbox settings). Log when each was confirmed. Say in the summary that the plan and its settings were declared by the user. For a commercial plan, ask what the user relied on, such as the terms or a zero-retention agreement, before releasing restricted documents.

findings.title: The 4.11 summary leaves out the local AI used for de-identification and covers the case, not the filed document
findings.evidence: The answer to "Which tool?" names only "Claude (Claude Code, Pro plan)". The log also records "name model on · LLM host 127.0.0.1:11434", and PD 1.6 applies to AI whether or not it is called AI. The summary gives case-wide totals ("12 of 17 chronology entries") rather than an account of a particular filed affidavit.
findings.recommendation: List every AI component used: Claude, the on-device name model and any local language model. Offer a per-document provenance report generated on export, listing each paragraph's origin, edits, adoption attestations, the sources it cites and their verification state. That is what a registrar would ask for under 4.11 about a specific filing.

findings.title: Adopting Claude's wording may not meet PD 4.9 in substance
findings.evidence: The adopt dialog needs two ticks: "This is true, and it is from my own knowledge." and "It is how I would say it." Paragraph 3, "Adopted by you today", adds a detail ("Mia had been waiting since 3pm") taken from the text messages rather than the witness's own recollection. Adoption then counts toward the export gate passing.
findings.recommendation: Keep adoption, but put rewriting first: show the user's own version beside Claude's and suggest typing it out. Make "own knowledge" concrete for each fact, e.g. "Did you see or hear this yourself, or only read it in a document?". Facts taken only from documents should be stated as such or attached as annexures.

findings.title: Affidavits and evidence come from plain-text transcriptions without guarding authenticity
findings.evidence: Imports are "Drop .txt or .md files". The text messages exist only as typed lines ("14/03/2025 3:05pm Anna: Where are you?..."). Export is "Export with real names", put back from tokens, including form variants like {{father.title}} -> "Mr Okafor". Nothing links a quote back to the original screenshot or file, or confirms that quotes put back from tokens match the original text exactly.
findings.recommendation: Store or point to the original file (screenshot, PDF) for each document and remind users that annexures must be the originals, not casefile transcriptions (PD 4.6, authenticity). When a draft quotes a source, check the restored quote character-for-character against the original before export.

findings.title: Claude's assessments of the evidence come close to legal advice and are not labelled as such
findings.evidence: The issue is "raised by Claude". Claude's notes judge evidential weight ("Shows a pattern", "cooperative on this occasion"). Draft para 6 reads "Claude suggests: say what time, and why it suits the children." PD 4.17 says assessing a claim's strengths and weaknesses is a lawyer's role.
findings.recommendation: Label Claude's characterisations as "Claude's view, not legal advice". Point users to free legal help (Legal Aid, family law advice lines) when issues or merits are being framed. Make sure prompts about affidavit content never supply the factual answer.

findings.title: Records only default to restricted if the user marks them
findings.evidence: "New documents are" defaults to "Ordinary" for a whole batch ("Checking 5 of 7 · school-reports-term2.txt"). In the list, school attendance records are marked subpoenaed only because the user said so (D009). A batch dropped in with the default goes to Claude after review.
findings.recommendation: Ask for each document's source at publish time ("Where did this come from? My own, from the other side, from a subpoena or court order...") rather than relying on a batch default. Flag content that looks like produced material, such as subpoena cover sheets, "Produced under subpoena" stamps, family report headers or medical letterheads, before Claude can see it.

findings.title: The export gate and adopt attestations block action
findings.evidence: "Export with real names" is disabled while "! 2 paragraphs are Claude's wording (4, 5)". The Adopt button stays disabled until both attestations are ticked. Exports "download to your computer, never into the case folder", so Claude never sees the re-identified output.
findings.recommendation: Keep this, and extend the same gate to chronologies, outlines and letters.

findings.title: Chronology checking shows conflicting sources and invented people
findings.evidence: The checker shows the cited lines from both sources and notes "The affidavit names both children; the messages only mention Mia. Check that 'Mia and Lachlan' is right before verifying." Unknown tokens are flagged: "Claude may have invented someone". "If it changes later, it goes back to 'to check'."
findings.recommendation: Keep it. When an unknown token is close to a real role (here {{grandmother}} vs {{maternal_grandmother}}), show the near match, but make the user re-check the source rather than just remap the token.

findings.title: A tamper-evident AI-use log with a draft 4.11 answer the user can edit
findings.evidence: "Intact · 412 entries checked". The entries separate Claude's actions from the user's ("Claude added chronology entry #3", "You verified chronology entry #3"). The summary answers the four 4.11 questions and adds "Read it over and change anything that isn't right before you use it."
findings.recommendation: Keep it, with the additions above: a per-document report, every AI component listed, and the PD 5.4 settings.

lens: Automation bias and the meaningfulness of human checking (PD-AI 4.7): do the verify/adopt flows force genuine checking or invite rubber-stamping? Is the source evidence shown at the point of decision? Is it clear what has and has not been checked? How could the design make verification real (friction where it matters, sampling, comparisons, highlighting discrepancies) without being exhausting?
summary: The mockups take verification seriously in places. The best example is the Chronology side panel, which shows the cited source lines and a discrepancy note next to the Verify button. But that care does not carry through to where it matters most. In the affidavit adopt flow, the user ticks two checkboxes without seeing any source. Paste/Copy lets Claude's text leave the app with no checking at all. Verify is one action covering a compound claim, and the V/J/K keys make rubber-stamping quick. The design's own sample data shows the danger: Claude's paragraph 5 says Daniel 'agreed to take them' when the source only says 'Fine.', and paragraph 4 invents the mother's feelings, yet the screens offer both a route to adoption. The AI-use log then tells the Court the work was 'verified against the source lines', which the app cannot actually know. Verification needs to be per-claim, tied to sources, backed by mechanical discrepancy checks, and recorded honestly.

findings.title: Adopt flow asks for sworn-truth checkboxes without showing the source evidence; sample paragraph overstates its source
findings.evidence: Draft 'Adopt paragraph 5' panel shows only a truncated quote ('…at Dapto pool…') and two checkboxes: 'This is true, and it is from my own knowledge.' / 'It is how I would say it.' It shows no citations or source lines. Paragraph 5 claims the lessons moved 'from 22 March 2025, and Daniel agreed to take them'. The only source (Document D001 lines 5–6) is Anna saying 'Swimming is moved to Saturday 8am' and Daniel replying 'Fine.' Nothing says he agreed to take them or that the change took effect on 22 March.
findings.recommendation: At the adopt step, show the paragraph's cited source lines (as Chronology does) and the full text being adopted, not a truncated one. Split the paragraph into its claims (date, place, who agreed, what was agreed) and require each claim to be matched to a line or marked 'from my own memory'. Flag claims with no supporting line. Replace the generic checkboxes with a decision for each claim.

findings.title: The 'edit until it counts as your words' meter lets invented content skip adoption
findings.evidence: Paragraph 4 'Claude wrote this · editing' has a meter labelled 'Still like Claude's wording … 38% · will count as your words'. Claude's text includes 'because I was worried about how upset Mia gets when nobody comes'. That is a state of mind no source records (D001:3 is just 'this is the third time this term').
findings.recommendation: Keep the record that the paragraph started as Claude's text however much is reworded. A light edit should still go through adoption, or at least through fact-checking of every claim carried over. Also flag statements about the witness's feelings, motives or beliefs as 'Claude cannot know this; only you can say it'. Show the meter as information, not as a target to get below.

findings.title: Paste and Copy let Claude's text leave the app with no verification or record
findings.evidence: Paste screen: 'With real names' panel with a 'Copy' button. The only checking is a footnote: 'Check facts, dates and any law Claude mentions on AustLII before relying on them'. The citations '(D002:9; D001:1–2)' are plain text, not linked or resolved. The Log screen has no paste or copy event.
findings.recommendation: Turn the cited lines in pasted text into links that open the source beside the text. Mark each sentence verified or unverified, and copy unverified text with a visible marker (or ask for confirmation first). Record paste and copy events in the AI-use log. Otherwise this route quietly gets around the Draft export gate.

findings.title: One Verify button covers a compound claim, and the keys invite rapid rubber-stamping
findings.evidence: Chronology toolbar: 'V verify · J/K move' with a 'To check 5' filter. The entry 'Daniel collects Mia and Lachlan 90 minutes late from Kiama Downs Public School' contains at least five separate facts (date, person, both children, 90 minutes, school) checked by a single 'Verify V'. On Issues, Verify sits on the card with no keyboard friction but also no breakdown of what is being verified.
findings.recommendation: Make V do nothing until the user has looked at the source panel, for example after focus or a short scroll through the cited lines. Where the app's checks find a discrepancy, require the user to resolve it (edit, or confirm with a reason) before Verify works. Consider a confirmation after several verifications in a few seconds ('You verified 4 entries in 10 seconds — review?').

findings.title: Discrepancy highlighting is a real strength, but it appears only for the open entry and its source is unclear
findings.evidence: The side panel says: 'The affidavit names both children; the messages only mention Mia. Check that "Mia and Lachlan" is right before verifying.' The list rows show only 'to check'. Nothing says whether the note came from casefile's own checks or from Claude.
findings.recommendation: Generate these checks in the app, deterministically. Since everything is tokenised, the app can test whether each entity, date and number in the claim appears in the cited lines (e.g. {{child_2}} is missing from D001:1–2, and '90 minutes' appears only in D002:9). Mark mismatched words in the claim and show a discrepancy badge in the list. If any note comes from Claude, label it, because PD-AI 4.7 says not to rely on GenAI alone for fact-checking.

findings.title: Nothing separates what the source says from Claude's interpretation
findings.evidence: Issues, D001:6 'Daniel: Fine.' is annotated 'He agreed promptly to the swimming change — cooperative on this occasion.' D001:3 is annotated 'Shows a pattern — third late collection this term'. The source says 'third time this term' and does not say late collection. The chronology entry 'Anna messages that it is the third late collection this term' makes the same inference. One 'Verify' covers the quote, the stance (supports or undermines) and the characterisation together.
findings.recommendation: Split verification into 'quote is accurate', 'stance is right' and 'Claude's description is fair'. Show inferred words differently from quoted words. On Issues, show a line or two around the cited lines (Chronology already shows line 8 above line 9) so that 'Fine.' is read in context.

findings.title: Export gate checks authorship but not whether the facts were checked; adopted paragraphs aren't linked to verified chronology entries
findings.evidence: 'Ready to export?' checklist: '✓ All tokens recognised', '! 2 paragraphs are Claude's wording', '– Check every fact and date yourself before filing'. The last item is a passive dash, not a tracked check. No paragraph in the Draft shows citations or a link to chronology entries.
findings.recommendation: Link each Claude-originated paragraph to the chronology entries or evidence it draws on, and show their verified status inline. Block export, or require explicit acknowledgement, while an adopted paragraph relies on an unverified or 'can't verify' entry.

findings.title: The Court summary overstates what the app knows about checking
findings.evidence: 'How was its work checked? 12 of 17 chronology entries and 9 of 11 evidence links verified against the source lines. 1 affidavit paragraph adopted…' The log row records only 'You · verified chronology entry · #3 · D002:9, D001:1–2'. It does not record whether the sources were viewed, whether a discrepancy was shown, or whether edits were made.
findings.recommendation: Log what was on screen at verification: sources displayed, discrepancies flagged and how each was resolved, any edits. Word the summary only as strongly as that record supports, e.g. 'marked verified with the cited lines shown; 1 discrepancy corrected'. Also state what was not checked, including the 5 unverified entries and anything copied from Paste. Under PD-AI 4.4 an overstated certificate is itself a risk.

findings.title: No flow for checking legal citations or quotes as PD-AI 4.7 requires
findings.evidence: The only reference to case law or legislation checking is the Paste footnote 'Check facts, dates and any law Claude mentions on AustLII'. No screen detects citations to cases or Acts, and none has a 'citation checked' state.
findings.recommendation: Detect case and legislation citations and quotes in Claude's output. List them in a 'Law to check' panel with an AustLII search link and fields for 'exists' and 'says what Claude claims', and record the results in the log. Block adoption or export of text containing an unchecked citation.

findings.title: No sampling or proportionality: everything gets the same light-touch check
findings.evidence: Chronology entries, evidence links and affidavit paragraphs all use the same one-click Verify or two-checkbox Adopt. Nothing scales checking to how the item will be used: chronology notes for the user's own orientation versus words in a sworn affidavit.
findings.recommendation: Tier the friction. Items that feed an affidavit or filed document get a full claim-by-claim check. Items used only to organise the case get a light check with random spot-checks, e.g. re-open one verified item in five for a fresh look. The burden stays manageable and the checking stays meaningful where it matters.

findings.title: Verified status doesn't reset when the source document changes
findings.evidence: Chronology footnote: 'If it changes later, it goes back to "to check".' The verified entry '2025-02-11 … D006:3–9' cites D006, which Documents flags 'Contains a value you added later · re-review'. Nothing shows whether a re-review or edit of the source document resets entries that cite it.
findings.recommendation: When a cited document is re-reviewed or its lines change, return dependent chronology entries, evidence links and adopted paragraphs to 'to check' and log why.

findings.title: Some Claude outputs have no verification state at all
findings.evidence: Issues header: 'raised by Claude · you verified the issue'. It is unclear what verifying an issue means. The 'Claude's notes' block ('The other two late collections this term aren't in any document…') has no verify status. Claude's issue description is also unverified prose.
findings.recommendation: Give every piece of Claude-authored content (descriptions, notes, issue framing) a visible unverified or verified state, or label it 'Claude's suggestion, not evidence'. Define what 'verify issue' means, e.g. 'this issue is relevant to my case', separately from fact verification.

findings.title: Strength: source shown at the point of decision, and the invented token is flagged
findings.evidence: Chronology aside 'Does the source say this?' shows D002 line 9 (with line 8 for context) and D001 lines 1–2 beside 'Verify'. The '{{grandmother}}' entry is marked 'can't verify · Claude may have invented someone', and Paste repeats this as an alert.
findings.recommendation: Use this pattern in Issues, the Draft adopt flow and Paste, where it is currently missing.

lens: Privacy and re-identification from the user's side: can the de-identified copy still identify people through quasi-identifiers or circumstantial details (rare events, small towns, occupations, dates, relationships)? Could real names leak via the UI (window titles, screenshots, exports, clipboard, notifications, file names, error messages)? Does the design make clear exactly what Claude can and cannot see, and what is withheld? What should the review step catch that it does not?
summary: For direct identifiers, the design is strong. Names, addresses, schools, businesses, Medicare/TFN/ABN numbers, dates of birth and the court file number become tokens. The user can compare "Original" and "As Claude sees it" side by side. The vault is blocked for Claude Code, and a cloud model posing as a local one is caught and refused. The weak points are details that are not direct identifiers and text that reaches Claude by routes other than the review step. Nothing in the review prompts the user to look for circumstantial details that could identify someone. "Leave as written" works on a person's name with no warning. Text the user types (draft paragraphs where "real names are fine", edits, chronology entries, evidence notes) reaches Claude's side, and no screen shows it being detected or reviewed. Document titles, author fields and file names have no visible token treatment. The import batch decides whether a document is ordinary or restricted, and the review screen never shows that setting. The app also never states in one place everything Claude can see: documents, derived records, token role names and metadata. Several routes take real names off the page (Copy buttons, exports, log download) without warnings.

findings.title: Review step only covers detections; nothing prompts a check for quasi-identifiers or circumstantial details
findings.evidence: The Findings panel groups only People, Places & organisations, and Numbers & dates. The only path for missed items is "Select text, then M to mark something missed". In the mock affidavit, "separated in June 2023", "On 14 March 2025", "90 minutes late" and "operates from the same address" all stay in plain text. Nothing flags occupations, rare events, distinctive medical details, kinship terms or small-community details. The Settings screen admits the default rules and name model miss these: the optional LLM "Catches nicknames, kinship terms and indirect details", and it is off or refused here.
findings.recommendation: Add a "Could still identify someone" pass before Publish. List the proper nouns, capitalised words, unusual nouns, numbers and dates that remain in Claude's copy. Prompt with a short checklist: job or workplace, small town, rare illness or event, nationality or ethnicity, distinctive incidents reported in the media. When no local LLM is running, say plainly that these details were not checked by machine. Offer a generalise action, for example a specific date to a month or a named job to "tradesperson", alongside tokenise.

findings.title: "Leave as written" on a person-name finding puts the name in Claude's copy without warning
findings.evidence: The undecided finding "Mr Okafor" (L7, found by name model) has two choices: "Apply ↵" and "Leave as written X". The single-key X shortcut and the J/K/N rapid-review flow make it easy to dismiss a real surname. Leaving it as written publishes the father's and children's shared surname. Publish is gated only on "1 left".
findings.recommendation: Treat leave-as-written differently by entity kind. For a person or place, require a reason ("not a person", "public figure", "a word, not a name") and show the exact text Claude will see. Never allow a single keystroke for a name that matches a known person's surname or alias. Record leave-as-written decisions on names in the AI-use log.

findings.title: Text the user types reaches Claude, but no screen shows it being detected or reviewed
findings.evidence: Draft: "Add a paragraph in your own words (real names are fine)". Paragraph 4's textarea holds real names ("I texted Daniel… how upset Mia gets"). Chronology has "+ Add entry" and "Edit". Issues has "Add evidence yourself". The brief says Claude reads and writes drafts, chronology and notes, so these records are shared with Claude. Nothing shows the user's text being tokenised, or what happens to names and identifiers that are not in the token key, such as a new person or a new phone number.
findings.recommendation: Run the same detection on every save of user-authored text. Show a compact "Claude will see" preview with highlights. Block the save, or quarantine the text, when it contains an unrecognised capitalised name or an identifier pattern until the user decides. Make "real names are fine" true by saying how: "we'll swap them for tokens; new names will ask you".

findings.title: No visible token treatment for document titles, author fields or file names
findings.evidence: Document titles include "Affidavit of Anna Thornbury" and "Affidavit of A. Thornbury". The Details form has Author = "Anna Thornbury". The import progress shows the original file name "school-reports-term2.txt". Real file names are often like "Mia_Okafor_NAPLAN.txt". The "As Claude sees it" view covers only the body text. Nothing shows what title, author or source file name Claude gets from casefile.
findings.recommendation: Run detection on titles, author fields, tags and original file names. Show them in the review and in "As Claude sees it", for example "Affidavit of {{mother}}". Never pass the original file name through; use the D-number. Add metadata to the leak check.

findings.title: Document kind (ordinary or restricted) is set for the whole import batch and is missing from the review screen
findings.evidence: Import has one control: "New documents are [Ordinary ▾]". It applies to the whole drop of "files or a folder". The Workbench review panel has Apply, Leave and Publish, but no Kind field. Kind can be changed only later, on the Document screen ("Kind: Ordinary / Subpoenaed"). That select also omits Discovery and Suppression, which the import offers. A subpoenaed record dropped in a mixed folder would be published to Claude as Ordinary.
findings.recommendation: Show the Kind setting on each document in the review step and make it a required confirmation before Publish ("Is this from discovery, a subpoena, or under a suppression order?"). Flag likely restricted material heuristically ("subpoena", "produced pursuant to", a letterhead from an agency). Use the same four options everywhere.

findings.title: Information from withheld documents can reach Claude through derived records
findings.evidence: Issues lists "Children's schooling and attendance · 3 supporting · withheld source". The Documents table shows "D009 Subpoenaed school attendance records" with its date and type. PD-AI 5.5 covers "information obtained through" subpoena or discovery, not only the files themselves. The design does not show whether Claude can see D009's title or metadata, evidence quotes from it, or chronology entries the user writes from it.
findings.recommendation: Treat anything that cites or quotes a withheld document as withheld too, and hide it from Claude, including its title and metadata. When the user writes an entry or paragraph citing a withheld source, warn: "This comes from subpoenaed material. Claude won't see it on your plan." Show a "withheld from Claude" badge on those items.

findings.title: No single, clear statement of everything Claude can see
findings.evidence: The per-document status ("Available to Claude", "Withheld · subpoena") is clear. Elsewhere: Unlock says only "Claude only ever works with the de-identified copy". No screen states whether Claude sees the token role list ("maternal_grandmother", "class_teacher", "fathers_business"), chronology, issues, drafts, notes, document metadata, the AI-use log, or the user's verification decisions. Chronology, Issues and Draft items carry no Claude-visibility indicator.
findings.recommendation: Add a "What Claude can see" page, linked from the header or Settings. List each category with on/off, and show an exact preview of the casefile command's output. Put a small eye or "Claude sees this" marker on derived records and drafts, as Document already does for documents.

findings.title: Copy buttons and exports put real names on the clipboard or disk without warning
findings.evidence: Paste has "With real names [Copy]". Chronology has "Export" but doesn't say where the file goes or whether names are real. Log has "Download". Draft has "Export with real names" and says "Exports download to your computer, never into the case folder", which is good. Clipboard managers and cloud clipboard sync keep copies. A user who copies real-name text and pastes it back into Claude defeats the tool entirely.
findings.recommendation: Label every copy and export with what it contains ("real names" or "tokens"). After a real-name copy, show: "Contains real names. Don't paste into Claude or other AI tools." Offer to clear the clipboard after a timeout. Apply Draft's "never into the case folder" rule to all exports. Default Chronology export to tokens or ask.

findings.title: Real names on screen at all times: window titles, screen sharing, OS screenshots
findings.evidence:
The app always shows real names (brief). Headings such as "

Affidavit of Anna Thornbury

" and "

Anna Thornbury

" would likely become native window titles, Mission Control and taskbar labels, and recent-documents entries. The mock s are generic ("Affidavit draft", "Document D001"), but nothing says the real window title stays generic. No notifications are designed. There is a Lock button but no auto-lock.
findings.recommendation: Specify that the native window title is always the neutral case label or a D-number, never a person's name. Keep person names out of OS notifications and recent-files lists. Add auto-lock on idle or sleep. Add an optional "show tokens" privacy mode for screen sharing or working in public.

findings.title: An alias added later is already exposed, but the design only says "re-review"
findings.evidence: "You added 'Annie' as another name for Anna Thornbury. D006 still contains it, so Claude can read it there." People: "'Annie' not yet replaced". Re-review fixes the copy going forward, but Claude may already have read D006. The log records reads by line range ("read document D001 lines 1–7").
findings.recommendation: Cross-check the log and tell the user whether Claude has already read lines containing the value ("Claude read D006 lines 1–12 on 3 Oct, which included 'Annie'"). Record the exposure in the AI-use log so the PD-AI 4.11 summary is accurate. Consider making D006 unavailable to Claude until it is re-reviewed.

findings.title: Two Advanced checkboxes can override the local-model protection with one click
findings.evidence: Under "Advanced" are two checkboxes: "Allow sending original documents to a remote model (not recommended)" and "This local server runs the model on this computer (for servers casefile can't check)". The second would bypass the very check that caught "deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud".
findings.recommendation: Require typed confirmation and name the destination host. Explain that the remote model receives the un-tokenised originals, including the children's details. Log the change prominently and show a persistent banner while it is on. Consider removing the remote option for restricted documents entirely.

findings.title: Free-text role names could themselves identify someone
findings.evidence: "Role name" is a free text input (value "mother") with "Rename everywhere", and the helper copy says "A relationship, never a name." The design shows no validation. Roles such as "class_teacher" and "fathers_business" are already descriptive, and a user could type "okafor_joinery" or "kiama_school".
findings.recommendation: Validate role names against the token key and the detection rules: reject any real value, alias or detected entity. Suggest generic role names. Warn when a role name narrows down someone's identity (job title, place).

findings.title: Original files and stray copies may stay where Claude Code can reach them
findings.evidence: Import takes ".txt or .md files or a folder" dropped from anywhere. Settings shows "Vault blocked for Claude Code: yes" and "Claude Code sandbox for this folder: on". No screen says what happens to the plaintext source files after import, or what happens if the user saves or exports an original into ~/Documents/casefile/case-1.
findings.recommendation: After import, tell the user the originals remain at their source location and offer to move them into the vault or delete them. Scan the case folder for plaintext files not created by casefile and warn ("This file in the case folder hasn't been de-identified; Claude Code can read it").

findings.title: Strength: the user can see exactly what Claude will see for each document, and the vault is technically fenced off
findings.evidence: "Original / As Claude sees it / Side by side" is available both in review and after publishing. "You see / Claude sees" columns use matched colours per entity. Settings shows "Vault blocked for Claude Code yes". The cloud-model detection explains that Ollama forwards to ollama.com despite the local address. Unlock advises "give it a neutral name" for the folder. The log records "leak check passed" on publish.
findings.recommendation: Keep these. Extend the side-by-side preview to metadata, user-authored text and derived records, as noted above. Show in the UI what the leak check actually checks.

lens: Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA): contrast on the dark theme (compute where you can from the hex values), keyboard-only operation and shortcuts, focus visibility, screen-reader semantics (landmarks, labels, live regions, tables), reliance on colour (especially the entity colour-coding and status colours), target sizes, motion, cognitive accessibility.
summary: On text contrast the dark theme is strong. Every entity colour, the amber and cyan status colours and the secondary greys pass 4.5:1 on their backgrounds; I computed 5.6:1 to 14.6:1. The failures are in other places. Non-text contrast on input and button borders is around 1.4 to 1.8:1. Line numbers, which are also citation targets, are at 3.1:1. The single-letter shortcuts cannot be turned off and include consequential actions such as X ("Leave as written"). Several key states are carried by colour alone or by hover/title only. The worst of these is affidavit-paragraph authorship in Draft, plus entity identity in reading views. Simulated deuteranopia makes child_2 and school almost identical (ΔE 2.4), and mother and child_1 (both solid-underlined people) very close (ΔE 4.6). The basics are good: labelled nav/aside landmarks, aria-pressed toggles, a labelled radiogroup for swatches, role=switch, role=status for import progress, and Workbench rows that highlight on focus as well as hover. These are a solid base, but the keyboard and screen-reader paths through the core review tasks (deciding a detection, checking a chronology entry, adopting a paragraph) are not yet specified well enough to pass WCAG 2.2 AA.

findings.title: Single-character shortcuts (J/K/N/M/V/X/1-3, /) with no way to turn off or remap, including consequential actions
findings.evidence: Workbench inspector lists 'J / K next / previous finding', 'N jump to next undecided', 'M mark selected text'; buttons show 'Leave as written X' and radio options keyed '1','2','3'. Chronology: 'V verify · J/K move'. Header search shows a '/' kbd hint. No setting for shortcuts appears in Settings.dc.html.
findings.recommendation: Meet WCAG 2.1.4. Add a Settings toggle to turn character shortcuts off, or require a modifier, or make them active only while the findings list or inspector has focus. Treat X (leave as written, which exposes the identifier to Claude) and V (records verification in the AI-use log) as consequential: provide undo and a visible confirmation toast. Check for conflicts with screen-reader browse-mode keys; NVDA and JAWS use letters such as K and N for quick navigation.

findings.title: Draft authorship (your words / adopted / Claude's, needs you) is shown only by a 3px coloured bar
findings.evidence: Each paragraph row is `` (white = yours), `#8CC4E8` (adopted) or `#E8A33D` (needs you), with an empty span and no text or ARIA. Paragraphs 1, 2 and 6 have no text label at all. Paragraph 5 is identified as Claude's only by the amber bar and number and the presence of an 'Adopt…' button. A legend at the top maps colour to meaning ('Your words · 3' etc.).
findings.recommendation: This is the PD-AI 4.9 control, so it must not depend on colour (WCAG 1.4.1) or be invisible to screen readers (1.3.1). Put a short text label on every paragraph ('Your words', 'Claude's wording — adopted', 'Claude's wording — needs you'), visually small but always present, or a visible icon plus an sr-only label. Also vary the bar's pattern (solid, striped, dashed).

findings.title: Entity colours collapse under colour-vision deficiency, and person-vs-person pairs have no non-colour difference
findings.evidence: Simulated CIELAB ΔE with the Machado matrices: deuteranopia child_2 #C6E07A vs school #D7D27A = 2.4; mother #F59BD0 vs class_teacher #B9C7D6 = 2.7; mother vs child_1 #5FD0C0 = 4.6; childcare #E6A9B0 vs mothers_home #9ED9B8 = 4.4. Protanopia: place_1 #8FCFE0 vs class_teacher = 3.7. Underline shape separates only people (solid) from places (dashed), so mother vs child_1 relies on hue alone. The code comment says 'Names and tooltips always say who it is', but in the real-text views a first name like 'Mia' or a title like 'Mr Okafor' does not show the role; that appears only in a `title` tooltip.
findings.recommendation: Don't treat hue as the cross-reference. Options: (a) an optional inline role badge after each highlighted name in reading views (e.g. 'Mr Okafor ·father'), shown on toggle or focus; (b) a per-entity glyph or monogram on the legend chip and in the mark; (c) pick the palette with a CVD check that keeps people far apart (ΔE ≥ 15 under deutan/protan). Keep the colour as a secondary aid.

findings.title: Entity info is hover/title-only on non-focusable marks, so keyboard and screen-reader users can't get it
findings.evidence: Workbench document text: `<mark title="{{seg.title}}" onMouseEnter=... onMouseLeave=...>` with no tabindex or onFocus. Document/Paste spans: `<span title="{{seg.title}}" onMouseEnter=...>`. The help copy says 'Point at a name or a token to see every place it appears'. `title` on a non-focusable span is not reliably announced and never appears for keyboard users (WCAG 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 1.4.13).
findings.recommendation: Make each detection in the review document reachable (roving tabindex within the document, or J/K moving real focus) and expose its meaning in the accessible name or aria-describedby (e.g. 'Mr Okafor, father, token father.title, decided'). Replace `title` tooltips with a focus-and-hover popover that can be dismissed, stays on hover, and has no timeout (1.4.13). Note the Workbench sidebar rows already use onFocus for highlighting; extend that to the text itself.

findings.title: Form-control and button borders fail non-text contrast (1.4.11)
findings.evidence: Inputs: border #2F353B on #121518 = 1.48:1 (on #171B1F = 1.40:1). Input fill #121518 sits on #121518 or #15191C, so the fill gives no boundary either. Secondary buttons: border #3A4148 on #121518 = 1.77:1 with a transparent background. Status-chip border #1E3446 = 1.43:1; amber card border #5A4114 = 1.92:1. Segmented-control selected background #262B30 vs #121518 = 1.28:1.
findings.recommendation: Raise interactive borders to at least 3:1 against adjacent colours (roughly #6B747C or lighter on #121518), or give inputs a distinctly lighter fill. Add a second cue to the selected segment (check icon, bold, or a 2px underline in #8CC4E8) rather than relying on the low-contrast fill. Chip borders are decorative because the text carries the meaning, so those can stay.

findings.title: Focus indicators removed or unspecified
findings.evidence: Search inputs: `outline: none` (Workbench, Documents); People filter `outline: none`; People role input `outline: none` inside the token box. The only stylesheet is `a{color:#8CC4E8}a:hover{color:#B7DBF2}`. There are no :focus-visible rules anywhere, and the custom buttons, segmented controls, legend pills and finding rows all rely on browser defaults. Only Unlock shows a focus treatment (a 2px outline at rgba 0.25 alpha, which is itself well under 3:1).
findings.recommendation: Define one global :focus-visible style that meets WCAG 2.4.7 and 2.4.13 (e.g. a 2px solid #8CC4E8 outline with 2px offset; 9.75:1 on #121518) and never remove outlines without a replacement (use :focus-within on the label wrapper for the search inputs). Show focused states in the mockups for the finding list, radio cards and segmented controls. Also make sure the sticky header and side panes don't hide focused elements (2.4.11).

findings.title: Chronology entries are not focusable; selection depends on J/K or a mouse click
findings.evidence: Each entry is a plain `<div style="display: grid; ...">`. The selected entry is shown only by background #1A2833 and an inset cyan bar, with no aria-selected or aria-current, link or button. The 'Check this entry' aside updates with no live announcement.
findings.recommendation: Render entries as a listbox or a list of buttons/links, with aria-current or aria-selected on the selected one. Expose status as text in the name ('to check', 'verified', 'can't verify', which already exist visually). Move focus to, or politely announce, the inspector heading when the selection changes.

findings.title: Text selection + 'M' is the only way to mark a missed identifier
findings.evidence: 'Select text, then M to mark something missed'. The document is a read-only grid of spans, and keyboard text selection inside non-editable content is unreliable without caret browsing.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit 'Add a missed name or detail' button that opens a field to type or paste the text (with find-in-document), alongside selection+M. This is also easier for motor- and cognitively-impaired users, and it covers the highest-risk failure: an identifier leaking to Claude.

findings.title: Line numbers (also the citation targets) at 3.1:1 contrast
findings.evidence: Line numbers use #5D666E on #121518 = 3.13:1 at 13–14px (Workbench numStyle, Document grid, Chronology figure '8 '). The product relies on line citations like D002:9 and the user is told to check them.
findings.recommendation: Raise to at least #8E979F (6.17:1). Line numbers are meaningful content here, not decoration.

findings.title: Dimming on hover/pin drops all other text below 3:1 and persists while pinned
findings.evidence: Non-active entities get `opacity: 0.35` (Document/Paste) or `0.4` (Workbench): computed 1.9–2.6:1 (father #9D8CFF at 0.35 = 1.88:1). Plain text dims to 0.45 (3.84:1). In Document and Paste the pin state ('Click to keep … highlighted') keeps this dimming indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Dim less (e.g. 0.6, about 4.5:1 for body text) or emphasise the active entity (thicker outline, bolder background) instead of fading everything else. While pinned, the rest of the document must stay readable at 4.5:1.

findings.title: Missing page headings and pseudo-headings styled as divs
findings.evidence: Workbench, Documents and Chronology have no h1. Section labels such as 'Needs decision · 1', 'People · 4', 'Ready to export?', 'Adopt paragraph 5', 'If the Court asks (PD-AI 4.11)', 'How Claude refers to her' and 'Does the source say this?' are `<div>` with uppercase styling. Issues correctly uses h2 for 'Supports · 5'.
findings.recommendation: Give every screen an h1 (it can be visually hidden on Workbench, e.g. 'Review D002 Affidavit of A. Thornbury') and make the uppercase section labels h2/h3 so screen-reader users can move by heading (1.3.1, 2.4.6).

findings.title: Workbench nav differs from every other screen and lacks aria-current; document-tab state is a bare '●'
findings.evidence: Workbench nav lists Documents, People, Chronology, Issues, Drafts, Log, with no Paste or Settings and no case name, while all wb/ screens list 8 items. 'Documents' is styled active but has no aria-current. The active tab 'D002 Affidavit of A. Thornbury ●' shows its unreviewed state only as an amber dot, which a screen reader announces as 'black circle'.
findings.recommendation: Use the same nav set and order on every screen (3.2.3) with aria-current='page'. Replace the ● with text or an sr-only label ('needs review'), and mark the document tabs up as a tablist or as links with aria-current.

findings.title: Side-by-side 'You see / Claude sees' view has no table semantics
findings.evidence: A CSS grid of spans: line number, real-text span, token span. The column headers 'You see' and 'Claude sees' are plain spans with no association. Linear reading interleaves both versions of each line with no indication which is which.
findings.recommendation: Use a real `<table>` with `<th scope="col">` for 'Line', 'You see', 'Claude sees' (or role=table/row/cell), so screen readers announce which column a cell is in. Offer the single-column views as the screen-reader-friendly default.

findings.title: No announcements for the outcome of key actions; aria-label on role-less divs
findings.evidence: Apply, Leave as written, Verify, Adopt and Remove have no status-message pattern shown. The '23 findings / 22 decided' and 'Publish · 1 left' counters are not live regions. 'Still like Claude's wording … 38% · will count as your words' changes while typing with no live region. `<div aria-label="Who is in this document">` and `<div aria-label="Who is in this text">` have no role, so the label is ignored. Good: import progress uses role=status and the unknown-token warning uses role=alert.
findings.recommendation: Add one polite live region per screen that announces results ('Mr Okafor set to father. 0 left to decide. Ready to publish.'; 'Entry verified, logged'). Debounce the wording meter's announcement. Give the legend containers role=group (or make them a toolbar) so the aria-label is exposed.

findings.title: Repeated identical button names ('Verify', 'Remove', 'Adopt…', 'Delete') with no context
findings.evidence: Issues shows two 'Verify'/'Remove' pairs on separate evidence cards; Draft has 'Adopt…', 'Rewrite', 'Delete' per paragraph. In a screen reader's buttons list they are indistinguishable.
findings.recommendation: Add aria-describedby pointing to the card citation (e.g. 'D001:3') or an sr-only suffix ('Verify D001:3 evidence', 'Adopt paragraph 5').

findings.title: Cognitive load and jargon for a stressed self-represented user
findings.evidence: Copy includes 'rules · name model', 'Language model refused', 'deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud forwards to ollama.com', 'Model checked against its fingerprint', 'leak check passed', 'LLM host 127.0.0.1:11434', token syntax '{{father.title}}'. The Workbench shows three panes, a hover-linked colour system and seven shortcuts at once. The Draft 'Adopt' button is disabled with no stated reason (it needs both checkboxes ticked).
findings.recommendation: Use plain language as the default (e.g. 'Extra name-finder: off — the one you chose would send text to the internet'), with technical detail under 'Details'. State why disabled controls are disabled ('Tick both boxes to adopt'). Consider a guided 'next undecided' mode on the Workbench that hides the shortcut list and shows one decision at a time (WCAG 3.3.2; COGA guidance).

findings.title: Amber means both 'needs you' and 'Claude', and some entity colours sit close to reserved status colours
findings.evidence: In the Log, the 'Claude' who-cell is #E8A33D, the same amber used for 'to check' and warnings. Normal-vision ΔE: childcare #E6A9B0 vs error #F4B5AE = 8.5; place_1 #8FCFE0 vs status cyan #8CC4E8 = 11.6. The People comment says swatches 'avoid the reserved status colours', but Dapto's #8FCFE0 is effectively the 'verified/available' cyan.
findings.recommendation: Give Claude's authorship a neutral marker (icon + text) rather than warning amber. Move place_1 and childcare away from the cyan and red status hues, and validate the full palette against the status colours, not just against each other.

findings.title: Strong text-contrast palette and good landmark/ARIA foundations
findings.evidence: Computed: body #E3E6E9 14.6:1, secondary #A7AFB7 8.25:1, hints #8E979F 6.2:1, amber 8.5:1, cyan 9.75:1, primary button text 9.4:1, entity colours on their 12% tints 5.6–9.6:1, undecided mark #FFE6BD on #5A4114 7.9:1. Also: labelled nav/aside landmarks, aria-pressed on view toggles and legend pills, a role=radiogroup with named swatches ('Pink (current colour)'), role=switch, a fieldset/legend for 'Which person?', 44px primary targets, people (solid) vs places (dashed) underline shapes, and Workbench finding rows that highlight on focus as well as hover.
findings.recommendation: Keep these as the baseline and carry them into the fixes above. Status words are already written beside the colour on most status cells ('verified', 'to check', 'can't verify'); apply the same approach to the Draft authorship bar and to entity identity.

lens: The workflow from Claude Code's side. Also read the CLI and its guidance in the repository: src/cli/commands.ts and src/core/guide.ts (the CLAUDE.md written into each case folder). Is the data model and command set good for an AI agent to organise a family-law case (reading at scale, citing, chronology, issues, drafting)? What would Claude need but cannot do? Where would it likely go wrong or produce low-quality work? How does what Claude produces surface in the app screens — is anything Claude can write not reviewable in the UI?
summary: From Claude Code's side, the CLI is unusually well guarded. Claude cannot touch the user's content. Every chronology entry needs a line-cited source. Invented tokens are rejected, and every error message tells Claude what to do instead. The screens let the user check chronology entries and evidence against the cited source lines. Where it falls short: the data model gives Claude too little context to write good family-law material. It cannot tell who the entities are (their relationships, the children's ages, which child is which). Affidavit paragraphs cannot cite anything. A chronology entry cannot record who says something happened. Search is weak once there are many documents. Several things Claude can write never appear in the screens. These are notes on documents, chronology entries, drafts and the case; evidence marked "context"; document details Claude set; and files Claude writes straight into the folder. Claude can also delete work the user has already verified or adopted, and deleting a Claude issue also deletes evidence the user added to it. The likeliest real-world mistakes are Claude swapping two valid tokens (the two children), stating one party's allegation as fact, and claiming something "isn't in any document" from search results that were cut off. Neither the CLI nor the screens catch these well.

findings.title: Claude can delete verified/adopted work, and deleting an issue cascades to the user's own evidence
findings.evidence: commands.ts `chrono rm`, `evidence rm`, `para rm` and `issue rm` check only created_by/author === 'claude', not verified_at or adopted_at. publicdb.ts deleteIssue runs `DELETE FROM issues WHERE id = ?`, and the evidence table is `issue_id ... REFERENCES issues(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`. So `casefile issue rm 1` on the Claude-raised 'Reliability of changeovers' issue (Issues screen: 'raised by Claude · you verified the issue') would also delete the verified D002:9 and D001:1–2 evidence and anything the user added through 'Add evidence yourself'. The Chronology filters are only 'All / To check / Verified', so a removed entry just disappears. The Log's Court summary counts would silently change.
findings.recommendation: Make the CLI refuse to remove anything verified or adopted, and anything containing user rows (evidence the user added). Have Claude suggest the removal with `note add` instead. In the app, soft-delete Claude removals into a 'Removed by Claude' view where the user can restore them, and show them in the Log.

findings.title: Affidavit and draft paragraphs carry no citations, so the user cannot check draft facts against the sources
findings.evidence: `para add DRAFT --text T [--after PARA]` has no --source, and the paragraphs table has no source column. CLAUDE.md rule 3 'Cite everything' covers only chronology entries and evidence. On the Draft screen, paragraph 3 ('On 14 March 2025 Daniel collected the children 90 minutes late...') and the unadopted paragraph 5 have no link to D002:9 or D001:5–6. The Adopt dialog asks 'This is true, and it is from my own knowledge' but shows no source lines, unlike the Chronology aside. Nothing models annexures, which affidavits normally use for text messages.
findings.recommendation: Add `--source ID:A-B` (repeatable) to `para add` and `para edit`, store the sources per paragraph, and show the cited lines in the Draft screen and the Adopt panel the same way the Chronology aside does. Consider annexure references so the exported affidavit can list annexures.

findings.title: Entities give Claude no context (relationships, ages, which child is which), so valid-token swaps are likely and nothing catches them
findings.evidence: The schema is `CREATE TABLE entities (role TEXT PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT NOT NULL)`, and `casefile entities` prints only TOKEN, KIND and the name forms. Dates of birth are tokenised (Workbench: 'born {{child_1.dob}}'), so Claude cannot work out the children's ages, even though ages matter in a parenting matter. The tokens {{child_1}} and {{child_2}} are opaque. checkTokens only rejects unknown tokens, so swapping {{child_1}} and {{child_2}} passes, and the screens then show only real names, so the user sees a plausible sentence. The Chronology hint ('the messages only mention Mia') shows the risk is real, but its author (app or Claude) is not stated.
findings.recommendation: Let the user give each entity a short de-identified description that `casefile entities` returns, e.g. 'elder child, girl, age 8, Year 3' or 'mother's mother'. In the verify panels, automatically flag any entity in Claude's text that does not appear in the cited lines.

findings.title: The Chronology screen's 'Unknown token' state cannot happen through the CLI, and the real failure mode is not designed for
findings.evidence: The Chronology row shows 'Grandmother {{grandmother}} starts Wednesday pickups' with 'Unknown token · Claude may have invented someone' and 'can't verify'. But commands.ts calls checkTokens on every chrono add/edit and fails with 'unknown token ... Run "casefile entities" for valid tokens.' So Claude cannot store this entry. People also lists the real role as {{maternal_grandmother}}. The state is reachable only if an entity is renamed or removed later. The Paste screen does legitimately need it, because chat output isn't validated.
findings.recommendation: Keep the unknown-token state for Paste and for entities renamed or removed after the fact, and word it accordingly. Spend the Chronology screen's error design on the failures that can actually happen: a valid token not found in the cited lines, a date not in the source, a source range that doesn't mention the event.

findings.title: Most Claude notes have nowhere to appear: only issue and paragraph notes surface
findings.evidence: `note add --on` accepts case, doc:ID, chrono:N, issue:N, draft:N and para:N. Every CLI refusal tells Claude to use it ('Suggest a change with: casefile note add --on chrono:N ...'), and CLAUDE.md rule 5 says 'Prefer casefile note add'. Only Issues ('Claude's notes') and Draft (paragraph 6 'Claude suggests: ...') show notes. The Chronology aside, the Document aside and Documents have no notes area, and case-level notes appear nowhere. Notes have no resolved or dismissed state.
findings.recommendation: Show notes in the Chronology and Document asides, at draft level, and in a case-level 'From Claude' inbox. Give notes a done/dismiss action, and count open notes in the 'Claude's recent work' panel.

findings.title: Evidence with stance 'context' has no place on the Issues screen
findings.evidence: The CLI accepts `--stance supports|undermines|context`. The Issues screen shows only 'Supports · 5' and 'Undermines · 1' sections, and the list summaries count only 'supporting' and 'against'. Context links Claude adds are never shown for review.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Context' section (or a stance filter) with the same Verify/Remove controls, and include context items in the list counts and the 'to check' badge.

findings.title: Document details and tags that Claude sets are shown as fact, with no provenance or check
findings.evidence: `docs meta ID --title --type --date --author-role --source` lets Claude set metadata (the store records meta_by='claude'), and `tag add` records created_by. The Documents table (Title/Date/Type) and the Document 'Details' form (Type 'messages', Date '2025-03-15', Author 'Anna Thornbury') don't show who set the values or whether they were checked. A wrong document date or author feeds into Claude's chronology. D001's single date of 2025-03-15 also covers messages dated 14–29 March.
findings.recommendation: Mark Claude-set fields ('set by Claude · check') with a one-click confirm, and show tag provenance on hover. Consider a date range for message bundles.

findings.title: Claude's output outside the CLI (files it writes, chat analysis) is not logged, not marked unverified, and not visible in the app
findings.evidence: The sandbox allows writes anywhere in the case folder; denyWrite covers only ./vault and the app folders. Claude Code habitually writes working files (chronology.md, analysis.md, draft-affidavit.md) and gives long analyses in the terminal. CLAUDE.md says 'Use the casefile CLI for everything' but never forbids writing files. None of this reaches the AI-use log or the 'If the Court asks (PD-AI 4.11)' summary; the only way to view it with real names is to paste it by hand into Paste. There is no command for long-form output such as a case summary or analysis.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit CLAUDE.md rule: no files in the case folder, and anything for the user goes through casefile. Back it with denyWrite on the case root (temp only). Add a `casefile report add --title T --text -` (or an 'analysis' draft kind) that appears in the app as unverified Claude work and is counted in the Log summary.

findings.title: Search is too blunt for reading at scale and invites false 'not in any document' claims
findings.evidence: PublicStore.search quotes each word and ANDs them, so there is no phrase, OR or prefix search. It has no doc, type or date filter, a 50-row limit, and no total count or offset. A token such as {{father}} becomes the FTS term 'father', which also matches ordinary prose ('the father'). The Issues screen's Claude note 'The other two late collections this term aren't in any document' is the kind of negative claim the tool cannot reliably support.
findings.recommendation: Return the total match count and support --offset, --doc/--type/--tag/--from/--to filters, phrase queries and token-exact matching. Add a CLAUDE.md rule that negative claims must state the searches run, and that withheld documents were not searched.

findings.title: The chronology model and the guidance let Claude state one party's allegations as neutral fact
findings.evidence: The chronology table has only event_date, description and sources: no 'asserted by', disputed flag, end date or link to issues. The screen shows 'Daniel collects Mia and Lachlan 90 minutes late' as a plain event, sourced from D002 (the mother's affidavit) and a text message. CLAUDE.md gives no guidance on neutral, attributed wording, and nothing on periods (e.g. who the children lived with from June 2023), which partial dates like '2023-06' can't express.
findings.recommendation: Add CLAUDE.md guidance on attributing contested events ('{{mother}} says...') and quoting rather than characterising. Consider optional fields: asserted_by, disputed, end_date, and links from chronology entries to issues.

findings.title: There is no feedback loop: Claude never learns why the user rejected or changed its work
findings.evidence: The Chronology aside offers Verify/Edit/Delete, and Issues offers Verify/Remove, with no reason captured. The log records only e.g. `chronology_deleted {id}`. No screen lets the user leave a note for Claude, though the notes table supports created_by='user'. A new Claude session starts from CLAUDE.md alone and will repeat mistakes.
findings.recommendation: Make the reason optional on delete or reject, and store it as a user note on the target. Add a 'Note to Claude' field on items and at case level. Add a `casefile review` (or `feedback`) command listing the user's decisions and notes since Claude's last session, and point to it in CLAUDE.md.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md and the settings don't address legal-advice limits or web access (PD-AI 4.17, 5.4)
findings.evidence: Rule 6 only says to flag legislation and cases for checking on AustLII. Nothing tells Claude not to assess the strength of the case or predict outcomes, which PD-AI 4.17 reserves to lawyers. PD-AI 5.4 asks users to disable web search where possible. CLAUDE_SETTINGS has no deny for WebSearch/WebFetch, and the Settings 'Claude Code' section checks only the CLI, the vault block and the sandbox.
