findings.recommendation: Deny WebSearch/WebFetch by default (or make it an explicit setting with a status row). Add a rule: organise and draft, don't predict outcomes or advise on prospects, and give an AustLII or Federal Register reference for any law cited.

findings.title: Claude's drafts other than affidavits (outline, letter, submission) have no review state in the UI
findings.evidence: `draft new --kind affidavit|outline|submission|letter|other` is available to Claude. The Draft sidebar shows 'Case outline · 14 paragraphs' and 'Letter to the other side · 5 paragraphs' with no count of Claude-written or unchecked paragraphs. Only the affidavit gets the 'needs you' badge and export gating. PD-AI 4.7's fact-check duty applies to any AI content, and a letter goes to the other side.
findings.recommendation: Show Claude authorship and a 'checked' state on every paragraph of every draft kind. For outgoing kinds, require a lighter 'I've checked this' step before export.

findings.title: An edit that goes back to 'to check' gives no diff, and the rewrite measure may count additions as the user's own words
findings.evidence: The Chronology footer says 'If it changes later, it goes back to "to check"', but nothing shows what Claude changed. rewriteSimilarity is an order-blind word-bag Dice score with REWRITE_THRESHOLD 0.5. On the Draft screen, paragraph 4 is labelled '38% · will count as your words' for what may be Claude's sentence plus an added 'because...' clause; appending enough new words can flip authorship. The mockup doesn't show Claude's original, so this is uncertain.
findings.recommendation: Show a diff against the last verified or adopted version. For authorship, measure how much of Claude's text is kept, not just overall overlap.

findings.title: Strength: the CLI's provenance rules give Claude actionable redirects
findings.evidence: Claude cannot edit or remove user content, and each refusal names the alternative ('Paragraph N is the user's own words; Claude cannot edit it. Suggest changes with: casefile note add --on para:N ...'). Claude chronology entries must cite at least one source. Source ranges are checked against the document's line count and withheld status. Every Claude write is logged and marked 'unverified'. --json is on every command, and '--text -' avoids shell-quoting problems.
findings.recommendation: Keep this pattern and extend it to the gaps above (verified or adopted deletions, paragraph sources).

findings.title: Strength: the source-side verification surfaces match Claude's citations well
findings.evidence: The Chronology aside 'Does the source say this?' shows the exact cited lines (D002 line 9, D001 lines 1–2) next to Claude's sentence. Issues show each evidence link as a quote of the cited lines. The Document aside lists 'Cited in' and a 'Claude's use of this document' trail. This makes D002:9-style citations checkable in one click.
findings.recommendation: Reuse this cited-lines panel for draft paragraphs and the Adopt dialog once paragraphs can carry sources.

lens: Scale, information architecture and navigation: how each screen holds up with 300 documents, 40 entities, 250 chronology entries, 30 issues, several drafts. Search, filtering, sorting, bulk review, cross-linking between screens, keyboard navigation, performance-sensitive patterns (e.g. side-by-side of long documents).
summary: The screens are built and checked against a case of about 16 documents, 13 entities, 17 chronology entries, 4 issues and 3 drafts. Most list screens would break down well before the 300 documents, 250 chronology entries and 30 issues this angle asks about. Workbench and Chronology have good keyboard flows, and Document's "Cited in" backlinks are good. But search appears only on two screens. Filtering is mostly status-only. No table can be sorted and nothing can be bulk-selected. Many cross-references are plain text or typed IDs, not links. Several things should be designed in before build: a single place to see everything waiting to be checked, filters by person, document and issue on Chronology, Issues and Log, and pickers in place of typed citations.

findings.title: Global search exists on only two screens and its results are never designed
findings.evidence: The header input 'Search everything' with a '/' shortcut appears only in Workbench.dc.html and Documents.dc.html. The headers of Chronology, Issues, Drafts, Log, People, Paste and Settings have only the case name, the nav and 'Lock'. No screen shows search results: whether they cover document text, chronology, issues and drafts, how they are grouped, or whether they search real names or tokens.
findings.recommendation: Put the same search (and '/') in every header, or use a command palette (Cmd-K). Design a results view grouped by type (documents with line hits, chronology entries, issues, draft paragraphs, people), searching real names and aliases. Each result should open the target at its line or entry. Once a case reaches 300 documents, search becomes the main way to find things.

findings.title: No single place shows everything waiting to be checked
findings.evidence: Things to check are spread across screens. Documents' right rail says '5 chronology entries and 2 evidence links to check' but links only to 'Open chronology'. Issues shows '2 to check' only for the selected issue in its sidebar. Drafts shows 'affidavit · 2 need you'. Documents shows 'Needs review 2' and a single 'Re-review D006' card. The top nav has no counts.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'To check' view, or counts on the nav items (e.g. Chronology 5, Issues 2, Drafts 2, Documents 2), that lists every unverified item across the case. Let J/K and V step through them across screens. With 30 issues, each holding a few unchecked links, nobody will find them by opening each issue in turn.

findings.title: Chronology can only be filtered by status, which won't work for 250 entries
findings.evidence: The only controls are 'All 17 / To check 5 / Verified 12', a fixed '2023-06 → 2025-05' span, '+ Add entry' and 'Export'. There is no search, no filter by person, document, issue or source, no date-range control, and no way to jump to a year (years are only static headings '2023', '2025').
findings.recommendation: Add filters for person (reuse the entity chips from Document/Paste), source document, linked issue and date range, plus a search box. Make the year headings sticky with a year jump list. Also allow filtering by who wrote an entry (Claude or you), since only Claude's entries need checking.

findings.title: Chronology filter state contradicts the list, and the 'can't verify' status has no filter
findings.evidence: 'To check 5' has aria-pressed="true", yet the list shows two 'verified' rows (2023-06, 2025-02-11) and a 'can't verify' row (the unknown-token entry). The counts 'All 17' = 'Verified 12' + 'To check 5' leave no room for 'can't verify'.
findings.recommendation: Make the list match the active filter. Add 'Can't verify' (or 'Problems') as its own filter with a count, so made-up or unresolved entries can't hide among hundreds of rows.

findings.title: Documents table has no sorting, no bulk selection and no paging, and its row order is unexplained
findings.evidence: The column headers (ID, Title, Date, Type, Claude, Cited) are plain text, with no sort buttons or aria-sort. Rows appear in the order D016, D015, D002, D001, D009, D006, which follows neither ID nor date. There are no checkboxes or bulk actions and no paging or row count.
findings.recommendation: Make the columns sortable and show the sort state. Add row checkboxes with bulk actions: set kind (subpoenaed etc.), tag, re-review and withhold. Show 'Showing N of 300', and keep 'Needs review' rows pinned as a labelled group above the sorted list. Also consider adding columns or filters for date range and people mentioned.

findings.title: Re-review after adding a name is designed for one document, not dozens
findings.evidence: Documents' 'Check again' card names one document: 'D006 still contains it' with a 'Re-review D006' button. People says 'Add them here and every document is checked again'. When a nickname like 'Annie' appears in 60 text-message documents, the user would face 60 separate re-reviews with no queue or batch view.
findings.recommendation: Design a batch re-review: a queue listing every affected document with its occurrences, the option to apply the new alias to all matches at once with a per-line review list, and a progress count. Withhold the affected documents from Claude until the batch is done.

findings.title: Workbench review has no queue between documents and its tab strip won't scale
findings.evidence: Workbench shows a document tab strip ('D001 Text messages', 'D002 Affidavit… ●', '+ Import'). Documents shows a batch import 'Checking 5 of 7'. Nothing shows which document comes next after 'Publish · 1 left', and a 30-file import would overflow the tab strip. The Workbench nav also differs from every other screen: it lacks Paste and Settings and the case name.
findings.recommendation: Replace the tabs with a review queue ('Document 3 of 30 · 4 undecided'), with Publish and next and a shortcut for the next document. Show queue progress, and use the same header and nav on every screen.

findings.title: Adding evidence requires typing document IDs and line numbers
findings.evidence: The 'Add evidence yourself' form is a text input with placeholder 'D004:12-15', a stance select and 'Add'. Nothing lets the user find the document or line, and no screen offers 'add selection to issue…'.
findings.recommendation: Let the user select lines in Document view and choose 'Link to issue…' or 'Add to chronology…' from there. In the Issues form, offer a document picker with search and a line preview. A self-represented user with 300 documents won't remember line numbers.

findings.title: Issues list has no search, filter or sort, and issues aren't linked to chronology entries or drafts
findings.evidence: The sidebar is a plain list headed '4 issues' plus '+ Issue', with no filter or sort and no keyboard shortcuts (unlike Chronology's J/K/V). An issue page shows Supports, Undermines and Claude's notes, but nothing links to the chronology entries or draft paragraphs that rely on the issue.
findings.recommendation: Add filter and sort (e.g. has items to check, has withheld sources, by evidence count) and the same J/K/V keys within an issue. Add a 'Used in' section listing related chronology entries and draft paragraphs. Showing filtered chronology entries beside an issue would also help when building an argument.

findings.title: Log shows times without dates, plain-text references and only one filter
findings.evidence: The header reads 'Intact · 412 entries checked', but the When column shows only times ('14:31', '13:40') with no date grouping. Detail cells use references like '#3', 'issue #1', 'affidavit #1 · para 3' and 'D001 lines 1–7', which are plain text, not links, and chronology entries are never shown with '#n' numbers elsewhere. The only filter is Everything / Claude / You.
findings.recommendation: Group entries by date with sticky date headings. Add filters for action type, document, date range and a text search. Turn every reference into a link to its target, and use the same IDs as the target screens. The Log is the evidence trail the PD-AI asks for, so it must be searchable once it reaches thousands of entries.

findings.title: Side-by-side document view and per-name hover highlighting may not perform on long documents
findings.evidence: Document renders each line as a grid row with both the real and the Claude copy. Each highlighted name has mouse-enter handlers that update state, and the whole render re-runs to dim or outline every match. Workbench does the same for every highlighted name. The mockups show 7 and 12 lines; a 400-line message export or a 60-page subpoena response would have thousands of highlighted names.
findings.recommendation: Render only the lines on screen. Apply highlights with a CSS class on the container, not by restyling every name. Add a document toolbar with find-in-document, go to line (reachable from D002:9 links) and 'next mention of this person'. Keeping both sides in one line-aligned row is good and should stay.

findings.title: 'In this document' chips and 'Where she appears' list will become a wall at 40 entities and 300 documents
findings.evidence: Document's legend shows a chip for every entity, with no limit. People's 'Where she appears' lists every document ('D002 … 6 times', 'D001 … 5 times') and the header says 'in 9 documents'. For the mother in a 300-document case this could be 200 rows, with no sorting or filtering and no links to related chronology or issues.
findings.recommendation: Cap the legend to the top entities plus a '+12 more' popover with a filter. On People, sort appearances by count or date and page them, add filters by document type, and add 'Chronology entries mentioning her' and 'Issues' sections. A link like 'Filter chronology by this person' would also help.

findings.title: Long drafts have no outline or way to jump to paragraphs that need attention
findings.evidence: The draft is one long column of numbered paragraphs. The export rail lists '2 paragraphs are Claude's wording (4, 5)' as plain text, not links. The adoption panel sits in the right rail, away from its paragraph. There are no keyboard shortcuts and paragraphs show no source citations or evidence links.
findings.recommendation: Make the paragraph numbers in the export checklist links that jump to each paragraph. Add 'next needing you' (N) and an outline or headings navigator for 80+ paragraph affidavits. Show each paragraph's sources (from chronology or issues) inline so the user can check facts without leaving the page.

findings.title: Strength: consistent keyboard-first review in Workbench and Chronology
findings.evidence: Workbench documents 'J / K next / previous finding', 'N jump to next undecided', 'M mark selected text', number keys 1–3 to pick a person, '↵' Apply, 'X' Leave as written and '⌘ ↵' publish. Chronology offers 'V verify · J/K move'. Findings are grouped with a 'Needs decision · 1' bucket and '23 findings / 22 decided' counts.
findings.recommendation: Keep this and extend it to Issues, Drafts, Documents (J/K over rows, X to select) and Log. Add a '?' overlay listing every shortcut.

findings.title: Strength: Document 'Cited in' backlinks and Chronology's inline source preview
findings.evidence: Document's 'Cited in' lists '2025-03-14 · Daniel collected the children late — chronology · lines 1–2 · verified' and 'Reliability of changeovers — issue evidence · lines 3–4 · unverified'. Chronology's check panel shows the cited lines from D002 and D001 inline, with a mismatch note about 'Mia and Lachlan'.
findings.recommendation: Use the same pattern everywhere: Issues should show which drafts use them, People which chronology entries mention them, and Log rows should link to their targets. Inline source previews should also appear on Issues evidence cards for citations that span many lines.

lens: Design versus what is built. Read the implemented app in src/app (api.ts, ui/*.js, ui/views/*.js) and the core APIs it uses (src/core/session.ts, drafting.ts, publicdb.ts — skim). List what the mockups show that is not implemented or not supported by the current API/data model, and the reverse (implemented capabilities with no design). Size each gap (S/M/L) in the recommendation.
summary: The colour system is the biggest gap between the mockups and the app. Every mockup except Unlock, Settings and Log gives each person or place its own colour, shared between the real name and its token. The app has nothing that supports this: the Entity type in src/core/entities.ts has no colour field, and every API response (show(), quote(), /api/reidentify, /api/docs/:id) collapses tokens into plain re-identified strings, so the client cannot tell which words are which person. The core fix is small and central. renderTokens in core/tokens.ts already walks every token, so it can emit segments of the form {text, raw, role, form}, and one client renderer can then serve all screens. Rolling out colour first is therefore realistic (about M overall). Beyond colour, several mocked screens rely on data the app has but does not show (log integrity, actor filter, Claude's per-document activity, edit endpoints). Two things need care: the Court summary must count verifications from signed vault checks, not /api/stats; and several safety states the app already implements (leak-check refusal, probe refusal, detector failures, a draft's kind changed outside the app, security log) have no mockup at all.

findings.title: Per-entity colour is not in the data model
findings.evidence: In the mockups each entity has a fixed hex colour, e.g. ENT = { mother: { color: '#F59BD0' }, father: { color: '#9D8CFF' } … }, and People.dc.html has a swatch picker. In the code, `interface Entity { role; kind; forms; aliases }` (src/core/entities.ts:20) has no colour. PATCH /api/entities/:role only accepts role, full, first, surname, title, aliases and kind (api.ts:384-402). NewEntityInput / PublishRequest carry no colour either. The client's only highlight classes are status-based (--known, --new, --ambig, --manual, --skip in style.css).
findings.recommendation: Size S. Add an optional `color` to Entity in the vault registry. Give each new entity the next unused palette colour at publish time, deterministically and skipping status hues. Accept `color` in PATCH /api/entities/:role and in PublishRequest.newEntities, and return it from /api/entities and /api/docs/:id/review. Keep the colour in the vault only; public.db does not need it. Do this first, because every other colour gap depends on it.

findings.title: API returns flat strings, so the client cannot colour names or link them to tokens
findings.evidence: In api.ts, show() returns `{ text: r.text, unknown, malformed }` and quote() returns plain(text). /api/reidentify returns a single `text`. /api/docs/:id returns `lines[].text = plain(t)`. The mockups need per-segment role data: Paste and Document build segs like `{ real, claude: token(role, form), title: name + ' · ' + token }` with hover linking, and Document/Paste show 'In this document … ×{{e.count}}'. renderTokens in core/tokens.ts:97 already loops over each token mark but only concatenates.
findings.recommendation: Size M, mostly mechanical. Have renderTokens also return `segments: [{text, raw?, role?, form?, unknown?}]`. Change show() and quote() to pass segments through, so every endpoint benefits at once. Replace richText/shown in ui/lib.js with a segment renderer that applies entity colour, the underline shape (solid for people, dashed for places, dotted grey for identifiers) and a title tooltip. The 'You see / Claude sees' columns and entity counts then come from one segment list with no second request. Keep the red unknown-token style for segments that do not resolve.

findings.title: Mockups are dark-only; the app has light and dark themes
findings.evidence: Mockup colours are pastels tuned for a dark navy background (e.g. '#C6E07A', '#D7D27A', '#9ED9B8' text on rgba(c, 0.12), row background #1A2833). style.css defaults to a light theme (--bg: #f6f5f1, --panel: #ffffff) and switches with prefers-color-scheme. Pale yellow-green text such as #C6E07A or #D7D27A on white will fail text contrast.
findings.recommendation: Size S–M. Define each palette entry as a pair of CSS custom properties: a darker light-mode value for text and underline, and the mocked value for dark mode. Store a palette index rather than a hex value on the entity, so a theme change never needs a data migration. Check each pair for contrast on both --bg and --panel.

findings.title: No rule for the colour palette once a case has more than about 10 entities
findings.evidence: People.dc.html offers 5 swatch OPTIONS (Pink, Lilac, Mint, Butter, Sand) and notes 'Options avoid the reserved status colours (cyan, amber, red) and the other entities' colours'. The mock case already has 6 people, 3 organisations and 2 places. A real case could easily have 30 or more people and places, and the backend's KINDS list has 10 kinds.
findings.recommendation: Size S, design decision. Specify what happens when the palette runs out: reuse colours across different kinds (the underline shape tells them apart), give minor people a neutral colour, or colour only the entities on the current page. Also decide whether the user's chosen colour must be unique.

findings.title: Review (Workbench) colours spans by entity; the app colours them by decision status
findings.evidence: Workbench marks each decided span with its entity colour and keeps a separate 'undecided' style, plus 'struck' for items left as written. reviewView in ui/views/docs.js colours <mark class='sp existing|new|ambiguous|manual|skip'> with a known/new/needs-decision/marked-by-you/left-as-written legend. Its side panel is a select dropdown, a 'Written as' dropdown and 'Apply', not the mocked list of numbered candidates ('Daniel Okafor father 1, Mia Okafor child_1 2…'). The data does support the mock: proposals with type 'ambiguous' carry `options`.
findings.recommendation: Size M, client only. Once colour exists, colour decided spans by their entity (new entities get a provisional colour that is sent with publish). Keep amber only for undecided spans and a struck style for skipped ones. Show the 'Which person?' numbered list from proposal.options. Add the grouped findings list (People / Places & organisations / Numbers & dates) from the span kinds.

findings.title: Review keyboard flow and 'As Claude sees it' preview are not built
findings.evidence: Workbench shows shortcuts 'J / K next / previous finding', 'N jump to next undecided', 'M mark selected text', 'X Leave as written', '↵ Apply', '⌘ ↵ publish', a 'View: Original | As Claude sees it | Side by side' toggle, and documents open as tabs ('D001 Text messages | D002 Affidavit … ● | + Import'). reviewView has none of these: it has a 'Mark selected text' button, no key handlers and only the original view with inline .tok badges. The client already has tokenFor(decision) for every span.
findings.recommendation: Size S for shortcuts and the before-publish Claude view (both buildable client-side from spans and decisions). Size M for document tabs, which are a new client navigation model with no API change. Shortcuts must not fire while focus is in an input.

findings.title: Leak-check refusal on publish has no mockup
findings.evidence: POST /api/docs/:id/publish can return 409 LeakError with `leaks[{text, field, reason}]`. docs.js then shows 'Not published: these would still identify someone', with 'Mark it' (marks every occurrence) and 'It's not identifying' per leak, and title leaks say 'Change the title below.' Workbench only shows 'Publish · 1 left'. The Log mock implies the check exists ('leak check passed') but no screen shows it failing. The document title Claude sees can also be edited before publishing in the app; the mockup does not show it.
findings.recommendation: Size S, design only. Add a mocked failure state to Workbench, plus a field for the title Claude sees. This is the last safety barrier before Claude sees a document, so it needs to be designed, not left as implementation-only UI.

findings.title: Probe-guard refusal when editing Claude's text has no mockup
findings.evidence: PATCH /api/chronology/:id, PUT /api/docs/:id/meta and PATCH /api/drafts/:id go through guardedSave(), which throws ProbeError when the edited text still names someone Claude's text named (ADR 3). Chronology mocks an 'Edit' button and Draft mocks inline editing ('Claude wrote this · editing … Save'), but neither shows the refusal. The app currently has no chronology edit UI at all, even though the PATCH route exists.
findings.recommendation: Size S. Design the inline error copy for a refused save, explaining that the user must retype the name rather than keep Claude's version. Then build the chronology Edit control on the existing PATCH route.

findings.title: Log mock needs integrity, actor filter and readable rows; the API mostly has them but the UI does not use them
findings.evidence: The mock shows 'Intact · 412 entries checked', an 'Everything | Claude | You' filter, and rows like 'read document · D001 lines 1–7' and 'searched “late” · 4 matches'. GET /api/log/verify exists but logView never calls it. store.listLog(limit, actor) takes an actor, but the /api/log route never passes it. logView prints `action.replace(/^cli:/,'')` and raw key: value detail. The detail is not re-identified, so a cli:search query would show tokens, not real names.
findings.recommendation: Size S. Call /api/log/verify for the badge (and design a 'broken chain' state, which the mock lacks). Pass an `actor` query parameter through. Add a table mapping action codes to readable labels. Re-identify string values in the detail before display.

findings.title: Court summary must not use /api/stats, which Claude can falsify
findings.evidence: The mock's 'If the Court asks (PD-AI 4.11)' panel says '12 of 17 chronology entries and 9 of 11 evidence links verified … 1 affidavit paragraph adopted, 3 written by me … 3 subpoenaed documents withheld'. No endpoint produces this summary. The obvious source, GET /api/stats, computes chronology_unverified from `verified_at IS NULL` in public.db, a column Claude can write. The app's real verification checks are the signed ones: isChronologyVerified, isEvidenceVerified, paragraphStatus.
findings.recommendation: Size M. Add a server-side /api/summary that counts using the session's signed checks (isChronologyVerified, isEvidenceVerified, isParagraphAdopted / hasUserAuthorship, isWithheld), and build the editable summary text from it. Fix or remove stats().chronology_unverified so nothing user-facing relies on it.

findings.title: People detail mock needs merge and occurrence counts, which the API lacks
findings.evidence: The mock shows 'person · in 9 documents', 'Where she appears: D002 … 6 times; D006 … · “Annie” not yet replaced 2 times', 'Merge with another person…' and 'Add another name … every document is checked again'. The API has renameEntity and updateEntity, and /api/audit reports per-document leaks, but there is no merge endpoint and no per-entity occurrence data. entitiesView is a single editable table with no detail pane. Saving an alias does not re-check documents; it only shows the audit notice.
findings.recommendation: Size S for occurrence counts (count replacements per role across vault documents, or derive them from segments). Size L for merge, which means rewriting tokens across public.db and every vault document, version-checked so existing verifications and adoptions are invalidated correctly; it could be deferred. Size S to show audit results per document on the Documents list ('Contains a value you added later · re-review'), as the mock does.

findings.title: Live 'counts as your words' percentage needs a preview endpoint
findings.evidence: Draft.dc.html shows, while editing, 'Still like Claude's wording 38% · will count as your words'. PUT /api/paragraphs/:id returns `similarity` only after saving (drafting.ts rewriteSimilarity against body and claude_body, REWRITE_THRESHOLD = 0.5). The comparison is between tokenised texts, so the client cannot compute it from the real-name text it holds.
findings.recommendation: Size S. Add a read-only POST /api/paragraphs/:id/similarity that tokenises the draft text and returns the score and resulting author without writing anything or attesting. Debounce it in the editor. Check with the ADR 3 probe-guard design that a non-recording dry run is acceptable (low confidence; I have not read the ADR).

findings.title: Chronology mock assumes export, filters, wider source context and a discrepancy note
findings.evidence: The mock shows 'Export', 'All 17 | To check 5 | Verified 12', a '2023-06 → 2025-05' range, V/J/K keys, entries grouped by year, and source panes showing the line before the cited line (line 8 above cited line 9). It also has the note 'The affidavit names both children; the messages only mention Mia'. The API has no chronology export, and quote() returns only the cited lines. Nothing in the data model generates that note.
findings.recommendation: Size S for filters, grouping and keys (client only). Size S to add context lines to citedLines and visually separate them from the cited lines. Size S–M for export with real names, downloaded and never written to the case folder, as drafts already are. Decide whether the discrepancy note is a Claude note (existing notes on chrono targets) or an app feature; if it is Claude's, label it as unverified Claude output.

findings.title: Claude Code status rows in Settings have no backing check
findings.evidence: The mock shows 'casefile command installed · yes', 'Vault blocked for Claude Code · yes' and 'Claude Code sandbox for this folder · on'. core/case.ts generates .claude/settings.json (sandbox, denyRead) when the case is created, but no API checks it later. settingsView shows only the cd/claude command.
findings.recommendation: Size S–M. Add a /api/claude-code/status that checks the casefile binary is on PATH and that the case's .claude/settings.json still matches the generated content (sandbox enabled, failIfUnavailable, denyRead for the vault). Design a 'changed / missing' state with a 'Restore' action, since these protections can drift.

findings.title: Built features with no mockup
findings.evidence: Built but not mocked: the Search page (searchView, GET /api/search; the mock only has a 'Search /' box with no results screen); GET /api/security-log (probe events, no UI anywhere); detector-failure and name-detection-off warnings in review; editing document tags and Delete document with confirmation; draft `kindChanged` (kind altered in public.db, shown as affidavit); draft kinds submission/other; the LLM API key field; the 'case open in another window' and passphrase rate-limit notices on Unlock.
findings.recommendation: Size S each, design only. At minimum mock the search results screen, a security-log section (on the Log or Settings screen), and the detector-failure and name-detection-off states in Workbench. These are safety-relevant and currently exist only as engineer-written copy.

findings.title: Unlock, adoption and export flows closely match what is built
findings.evidence: Unlock fields and copy (12-character minimum, 'If you forget it, the originals can't be recovered', neutral folder name) match renderLocked. The adopt dialog's two statements ('This is true, and it is from my own knowledge.' / 'It is how I would say it.') match adoptDialog and the adopt API's ownKnowledge/ownWords. 'Exports download to your computer, never into the case folder' matches exportDraft. The Claude-plan radio and LLM 'Not used: text would leave this computer' check match /api/settings/claude-setup and check-llm.
findings.recommendation: Keep these flows as they are; no backend changes needed.

lens: Devil's advocate: argue against the current design. What is over-built, over-complicated or solving the wrong problem for a single self-represented parent? What would a much simpler product look like that still meets PD-AI? Which screens or features would you cut, merge or defer? Be specific and fair.
summary: Taken together, these screens are a small litigation workbench: ten screens, more than nine nav items, per-person colour pickers, aliases and merging, a three-way view toggle shown on three screens, a gameable "% your words" meter, a language-model config with remote-model overrides, a plan switch that self-certifies, and a hash-checked log of 412 entries. The person using it is one stressed parent with one case. Very little of this is needed to meet PD-AI. What PD-AI requires is the core loop: de-identify and review, withhold restricted material, check every Claude output against its source, keep affidavits in the parent's own words, and be able to explain AI use. A much simpler product could cover that with about four surfaces: Unlock; Documents (import, review, publish, with a per-document restricted flag that always withholds); one "To check" queue that shows each Claude output with real names next to its cited source lines; and a Log page built around the court summary. Chronology entries, issue links and pasted text would all go through that one queue. On the affidavit, the design solves the wrong problem. Claude should not write paragraphs for the parent to adopt. It should prompt for detail while the parent writes, which is simpler and closer to PD-AI 4.9. Several parts are good and should survive any cut: the source-check panel, unknown-token detection, withholding restricted documents, and the "If the Court asks" summary.

findings.title: Claude-written affidavit paragraphs plus an 'adopt' and '% your words' system solves the wrong problem
findings.evidence: Draft has three authorship buckets ('Your words · 3', 'Claude’s, adopted by you · 1', 'Claude’s, needs you · 2'). There is a similarity meter, 'Still like Claude’s wording … 38% · will count as your words', with a 50% marker. There is also an 'Adopt paragraph 5' dialog with ticks for 'This is true…' and 'It is how I would say it.' PD-AI 4.9 says affidavit content must be 'expressed in the witness’s own words'.
findings.recommendation: Cut both the adopt flow and the meter. In an affidavit, Claude should never write the evidence paragraphs. It can propose an outline, list facts with citations, and give prompts like the one paragraph 6 already shows ('Claude suggests: say what time, and why it suits the children'). The parent writes every paragraph. This removes the authorship tracking, the threshold maths, the withdraw state and the export gate. It is also easier to defend under 4.9 than a percentage score that a user can push past 50% by rewording.

findings.title: Chronology, Issues and Paste are three separate verification surfaces for one job
findings.evidence: Chronology has 'To check 5' with Verify/Edit/Delete. Issues has per-evidence 'Claude · to check' with Verify/Remove. Paste shows Claude's text with real names and a warning about unknown tokens. The Documents sidebar sends the user to all of them: '5 chronology entries and 2 evidence links to check.' Each screen applies the same PD-AI 4.7 rule: check Claude's output against the source.
findings.recommendation: Merge them into a single 'To check' inbox. Every item would be one Claude output, whatever its type, shown with real names next to its cited source lines. Build it from the Chronology right panel ('Does the source say this?'). Each item would get Verify, Edit or Discard. Chronology and issue lists can then be read-only views of verified items, or exports Claude writes as files in the case folder.

findings.title: Issues screen goes beyond organising into assessing the strength of the case
findings.evidence: Issues are 'raised by Claude'. Evidence is sorted into 'Supports · 5' and 'Undermines · 1', and Claude adds commentary such as 'Shows a pattern — third late collection this term.' and 'He agreed promptly to the swimming change — cooperative on this occasion.' PD-AI 4.17 says that advising on 'the strengths or weaknesses of a legal claim' is the role of a lawyer.
findings.recommendation: Defer Issues from v1. If it stays, limit it to topic tags on chronology entries and drop the supports/undermines framing and Claude's characterisations. This removes a screen, a set of stance controls ('supports / undermines / context'), and a feature that a parent could easily read as legal advice.

findings.title: Per-entity colour system is over-built and will not scale to a real case
findings.evidence: Each entity has its own hue (ENT map: '#F59BD0', '#9D8CFF', '#5FD0C0', '#C6E07A', '#D7D27A', '#E6A9B0', '#9ED9B8', '#A9B8F0'…). People already lists 6 people, 3 organisations and 3 places, and has a 'Colour' picker for each person. Real parenting matters often involve grandparents, teachers, doctors, partners, caseworkers and police, so there will be 20 or more entities. Many pastel hues on a dark background become hard to tell apart well before that. The files do back up colour with names and tooltips ('colour is never the only cue').
findings.recommendation: Before rolling colour out to every screen, scale it down. Use colour by category (person, place, identifier), which the files already encode with solid, dashed and dotted underlines. Highlight one specific entity only on hover or pin. Remove the per-person colour picker. This gives most of the 'which token is who' benefit without making the parent manage a palette.

findings.title: Local language model setup, with a remote-originals override, is power-user scope and a safety footgun
findings.evidence: Settings includes 'Server address', 'Model', an Ollama cloud detection warning ('“deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud” is an Ollama cloud model…'), the command 'ollama pull qwen3:8b', and under Advanced, 'Allow sending original documents to a remote model (not recommended)'. The Documents sidebar repeats the same jargon: 'Language model refused · deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud forwards to ollama.com'.
findings.recommendation: Defer the optional language model. Rules plus the on-device name model plus mandatory human review already cover detection, and the 'Other names for her' alias feature handles nicknames. Remove the 'send originals to a remote model' toggle outright. A parent should not be one checkbox away from breaching PD-AI 3.3 (Safety) and 5.4. At minimum, keep the language model out of the Documents sidebar.

findings.title: Commercial-plan switch lets the user unlock restricted documents with one radio button
findings.evidence: Settings has two choices: 'Pro or Max (consumer)' and 'Team, Enterprise or API (commercial) · No training on your data under the commercial terms. Restricted documents are shared, de-identified.' The brief says the user's plan is consumer Pro/Max. PD-AI 5.5 requires the user to be satisfied that enforceable confidentiality terms apply and that the material stays within a closed environment.
findings.recommendation: For this user, cut the commercial branch and always withhold discovery, subpoena and suppression material. That removes a settings section and a branching state in Documents. If the branch comes back later, make it more than a radio button: for example, a confirmation that names the specific terms the user is relying on.

findings.title: Tamper-checked, fine-grained AI-use log is more than PD-AI 4.11 asks for; the court summary is the useful part
findings.evidence: The log shows 'Intact · 412 entries checked' and rows for every read and search ('read document · D001 lines 1–7', 'searched · “late” · 4 matches'), with Everything/Claude/You filters. PD-AI 4.11 only requires being able to explain whether AI was used, which tool, how output was checked, and how the principles were observed. The 'If the Court asks' panel answers exactly those four questions.
findings.recommendation: Make the four-answer summary the page itself. Keep the raw log as a Download only, and drop the visible integrity badge and the filters for v1. A parent never needs to browse 412 read and search events.

findings.title: Document screen duplicates Workbench; the three-way view toggle appears on three screens
findings.evidence: Both Workbench and Document have 'Original / As Claude sees it / Side by side' toggles and an entity legend. Paste has the same 'Claude’s text / With real names' pair and the same 'Show everyone' legend. Document's own sidebar ('How to read this') has to explain the colour-linking.
findings.recommendation: Make the post-publish document view the same component as the review Workbench, with editing locked and a 'Re-review' button. Default to the real-names view and offer 'what Claude sees' as one toggle rather than three modes. That gives one reading surface to learn instead of three.

findings.title: Token-key management (form variants, aliases, rename, merge) is more than v1 needs
findings.evidence: People shows 'Ways her name is written' with four forms (Full name, First name, Surname, Title + surname, each with its own token), 'Rename everywhere', 'Other names for her', 'Merge with another person…', a colour picker, and per-document counts. In Workbench, 'Mr Okafor' needs a 'Which person?' choice between father, child_1 and child_2.
findings.recommendation: Keep role naming and aliases. Aliases are a real gap, since 'Nicknames aren’t detected automatically'. Defer Merge and the colour picker. Consider generating the form variants automatically and showing them read-only. The parent's real job here is to confirm who each person is, not to curate a token schema.

findings.title: Navigation and keyboard model are aimed at a professional power user
findings.evidence: The top bar has Documents, People, Chronology, Issues, Drafts, Paste, Log, Settings, Search ('/') and Lock. Workbench's bar omits Paste and Settings, so the two navs are inconsistent. Shortcuts are shown throughout: 'J / K next / previous finding', 'N', 'M', '⌘ ↵ publish', 'V verify'.
findings.recommendation: Cut the nav to about four destinations: Documents, To check, Affidavit, Log (with Settings under it or behind the case name). Keep shortcuts, but show visible buttons first and shortcut hints second. A parent who opens the app weekly will not learn J/K/N/M/V.

findings.title: Two Claude workflows (Claude Code in the folder and copy/paste) with no clear primary
findings.evidence: Settings tells the user to run 'cd ~/Documents/casefile/case-1' and then 'claude' in a terminal. Paste exists to 'See anything Claude wrote with the real names back in', which implies Claude is also used elsewhere. The brief describes Claude Code as the way the product works. It is unclear where pasted text comes from and whether that use is logged.
findings.recommendation: Pick one primary path and design around it. If Claude Code is the path, Claude's outputs are already in the case folder, so Paste can become a small utility rather than a top-level screen. If Paste is meant for chat use outside Claude Code, the log and the withholding rules need to cover that path too. Unclear from the files, so low confidence.

findings.title: Strength: source-line check panel and invented-token detection
findings.evidence: Chronology's right panel shows 'Does the source say this?' with the cited D002 line 9 and D001 lines 1–2 inline, plus a note: 'The affidavit names both children; the messages only mention Mia.' Unknown tokens are flagged: 'Unknown token · Claude may have invented someone · can’t verify'.
findings.recommendation: Make this the core of the simplified product: one queue in which every Claude output is checked this way. It is the most direct way to meet PD-AI 4.7 in the whole design.

findings.title: Strength: withholding restricted documents and the 'If the Court asks' summary
findings.evidence: Documents has 'New documents are Ordinary / Discovery / Subpoenaed / Under suppression order' and shows 'Withheld · subpoena' on D009. Log has 'If the Court asks (PD-AI 4.11)', which answers the four questions from the log, with 'Read it over and change anything that isn’t right'.
findings.recommendation: Keep both in any cut-down version. They map one-to-one to PD-AI 5.5 and 4.11 and add little complexity. Consider asking for the restricted classification per document on import rather than as a batch default, so a subpoenaed file can't slip through under 'Ordinary'.

lens: Consistency with the product's own recorded decisions. Read the architecture decision records in docs/adr/ and docs/PLAN.md. Where does the design contradict, ignore or misrepresent a decision (e.g. what Claude can see, withholding, verification semantics, authorship/adoption rules, export rules, LLM endpoint handling, the AI-use log)? Where does the design promise something the decisions say is not possible?
summary: Most of the mockups follow the ADRs closely. Cloud-model refusal, the affidavit export gate, downloads-only export, "can't verify" for an unknown token, and the "a relationship, never a name" role rule all match the decisions. The serious problems are where the design claims more than the architecture can deliver, or opens a path the decisions close. Settings says the vault is "blocked" and the sandbox is "on", but ADR 3 says casefile cannot enforce or observe either. The AI-use log and its Court summary present themselves as complete and certain, which ADR 8 explicitly says they are not. The Paste screen produces Claude's text with real names and no authorship gate or log entry, which gets around ADR 9. The identifier tokens shown in the Workbench ({{mother.phone}}, {{child_1.dob}}) are malformed under the ADR 5 grammar. Several states the ADRs require the UI to show are also missing: failed detectors on the review screen, probe refusals and the security log, the "names are not checked" warning, and what is lost when withholding or re-review changes a document.

findings.title: Settings claims the vault is blocked and the sandbox is on, which casefile cannot know or enforce
findings.evidence: The Claude Code section shows status rows "Vault blocked for Claude Code: yes" and "Claude Code sandbox for this folder: on", with the copy "It ... works only through the casefile command." Unlock says "Claude only ever works with the de-identified copy." ADR 3 rule 4 says the permissions.deny rules "are not relied on" and any other program gets round them. The sandbox settings "are honoured by Claude Code, not enforced by casefile, and the user (or managed settings) can override them." The Consequences section says the guarantee does not hold against an unsandboxed same-user process, and that Claude Code has a shell, so it does not work only through the CLI.
findings.recommendation: Report what the app can actually check: "Sandbox settings written to this folder (Claude Code applies them; casefile can't confirm they're in force)." Drop "Vault blocked: yes" and "works only through the casefile command." Add the ADR 3/12 recommendation next to the language-model option: if you run Claude Code without the sandbox, use the name model only.

findings.title: The Paste screen is an export path for Claude's text with real names, with no authorship gate and no log entry
findings.evidence: Paste re-identifies any text Claude wrote and offers a "Copy" button under "With real names", and says "nothing is sent anywhere." ADR 9 blocks affidavit export until every Claude paragraph is rewritten or adopted, and logs both `exported` and `export_blocked`. A user can paste Claude's affidavit paragraphs here, copy them with real names and file them, which skips the PD-AI 4.9 gate and leaves nothing in the AI-use log. Neither PLAN.md nor any ADR records Paste as a feature.
findings.recommendation: Either record a decision for Paste (an ADR) or constrain it. Log each use (without the content), label the output "Claude's words, not for an affidavit", and point to Drafts for anything sworn. At minimum, say that text copied from here is not covered by the authorship check.

findings.title: Identifier tokens in the Workbench break the ADR 5 token grammar
findings.evidence: renderVals uses tooltip tokens such as `{{child_1.dob}}`, `{{child_2.dob}}`, `{{mother.phone}}`, `{{mother.email}}`, `{{mother.medicare}}`, `{{mother.tfn}}` and `{{fathers_business.abn}}`. ADR 5 allows only the forms `.first`, `.surname` and `.title`, and says "Anything else that looks like a token is malformed." src/core/tokens.ts has FORMS = ["first","surname","title"]. Identifiers are separate entities of kind phone/email/identifier/date_of_birth, named by a suggestion or `kind_N`, not attached to a person.
findings.recommendation: Show identifiers as their own roles (for example `{{phone_1}}` or `{{date_of_birth_1}}`, whatever the registry actually generates). If tying identifiers to a person is wanted, that is a grammar change and needs its own ADR. It also makes public which person each number belongs to, which ADR 3 treats as public role information and so needs a deliberate decision.

findings.title: The Court summary in the AI-use log says things the other screens show to be false
findings.evidence: Log's "If the Court asks (PD-AI 4.11)" panel says "Names and identifiers replaced before Claude saw anything; 3 subpoenaed documents withheld from Claude entirely." Documents says "You added 'Annie'... D006 still contains it, so Claude can read it there." Only D009 is marked subpoena; the other withheld documents' kinds aren't shown. ADR 7 says a withheld document still has a public row with a generic title, and Claude's earlier work from it stays. ADR 3/6 say name detection is optional, and NER is off by default (ADR 12). "Which tool? Claude (Claude Code, Pro plan)": the app only records `consumer` or `commercial` (ADR 7), so it cannot know Pro rather than Max.
findings.recommendation: Build the summary only from facts the log and settings record. Qualify it ("identifiers and the names known to casefile were replaced; 1 document had an unreplaced alias until [date]"), use "text withheld" rather than "entirely", give the counts by sensitivity type, and say "consumer plan (Pro/Max)". Flag anything open, such as a pending re-review, inside the summary.

findings.title: The log shows "Intact" with no limits, and presents CLI entries as a full record of what Claude saw
findings.evidence: Log shows "Intact · 412 entries checked". Document has "Claude's use of this document: read lines 1–7 ...". ADR 8 says verifyLog also reports forged entries and CLI entries still waiting to be countersigned. It also says CLI rows Claude alters or deletes before countersigning "cannot be detected; the chain proves the log as the app saw it." ADR 3 says public.db is readable by "anything else on the machine", so Claude can read text with its shell (sqlite or python) without a CLI log entry.
findings.recommendation: Show the pending-countersignature count and any forged rows next to "Intact". Rename "Claude's use of this document" to "casefile commands Claude ran", with a note that reads outside the casefile command aren't recorded.

findings.title: The review screen does not list failed detectors, though ADR 6 requires it
findings.evidence: Documents and Settings show the language model as "refused" (cloud model). ADR 12 says "A refusal is a detector error, which the pipeline reports." ADR 6 says "on import and re-detection the review screen lists them". The Workbench finding panel and inspector show no detector status. The Log import row says only "rules, name model · 23 found".
findings.recommendation: Add a detector-status line to the Workbench findings header, for example "Language model failed: cloud model refused. Nicknames and indirect details were not checked." Record the failure in the import log row.

findings.title: Editing Claude's text has no design for the probe refusal, and the security log appears nowhere
findings.evidence: Draft paragraph 4 shows "Claude wrote this · editing" with Save. Chronology offers "Edit" on Claude entries, and Document has an editable Details form. ADR 3 says such saves are refused (`ProbeError`) when the new text still names an entity that Claude's text named as plain text: "The user is told why and asked to remove the value or type a token." It also says "The user sees the probes via GET /api/security-log." No screen shows that refusal message or any view of the security log.
findings.recommendation: Design the refusal state for these edit surfaces, explaining why and offering to insert the token. Add a security or probe view, for example a section in Log or Settings, backed by /api/security-log.

findings.title: Re-reviewing D006 will reset verifications the design shows as safe
findings.evidence: Documents flags D006 "Contains a value you added later · re-review". Chronology shows the 2025-02-11 entry citing "D006:3–9 · Claude · verified". Under the ADR 8 amendment, verifications sign a hash of the cited tokenised lines, so republishing D006 with "Annie" tokenised will change those lines and put the entry back to unverified. The "Re-review D006" button gives no warning of this.
findings.recommendation: On the re-review prompt, list what will need checking again ("1 chronology entry and 1 evidence link cite D006 and will need checking again"). Mark those items as at risk while the re-review is pending.

findings.title: A withheld document shows details that ADR 7 says are removed
findings.evidence: The D009 row ("Withheld · subpoena") shows Date 2025-05-20 and Type "school records". ADR 7: whenever a document is published as withheld, its document details (type, date, author role, source) and tags are removed, and "Details the user sets on a withheld document therefore last only until it is next republished." Document's Kind select also offers only Ordinary/Subpoenaed and gives no warning that changing it withholds the text and drops details and tags.
findings.recommendation: Show withheld documents without public details, or say that these are kept only in the app. Warn when the sensitivity is raised (text, details and tags are removed from Claude's copy) and when the plan is switched back to consumer. Offer all five sensitivities from ADR 7 (none, discovery, subpoena, suppression, restricted).

findings.title: No warning that names are not checked when no name detector is on
findings.evidence: Every mockup shows the name model switched on. ADR 12 says NER is off by default. ADR 6 says the app warns "Only identifiers are checked automatically — names are not" when it is off, and ADR 3 rule 6 relies on that warning for titles. That state is not designed anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Design the default-off state: a persistent warning in the Documents detection panel and the Workbench header, with a one-click way to turn on the name model.

findings.title: The unlock screen has no lockout wait and does not say other programs can cause it
findings.evidence: ADR 13: "The wait is shown in the unlock screen (retryAfterSeconds from status) and in the 429 error, which says that any program can cause it." The Unlock mockup has no lockout or wait state. The 30-minute idle auto-lock is also not mentioned anywhere.
findings.recommendation: Add a lockout state ("Too many wrong passphrases. Try again in 1:20. Any program on this computer can cause this.") and a note about the idle auto-lock.

findings.title: Switching the Claude plan is a plain radio button, with no consequences shown
findings.evidence: "Team, Enterprise or API (commercial): ... Restricted documents are shared, de-identified." ADR 7: switching to commercial republishes restricted text to public.db. Switching back removes text, details and tags, but Claude's derived work stays. The change is logged. The mockup shows none of this and no confirmation. By contrast, ADR 12's remote-model opt-in requires explicit acceptance.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the change in a dialog that says how many documents become visible to Claude, or what will be removed when switching back, and that the change is recorded in the AI-use log.

findings.title: A draft whose kind was changed is not shown
findings.evidence: The drafts list shows kinds ("Case outline · outline"). ADR 9 says that if public.db's kind differs from the kind recorded in the vault, the app treats the draft as an affidavit and the API reports `kindChanged`. No state for this exists, so an outline that suddenly needs adoption would be unexplained. ADR 9 also says paragraphs from before attestation existed "need to be re-saved or adopted", and that state isn't shown either.
findings.recommendation: Add a badge such as "Kind changed outside the app; treated as an affidavit" in the drafts list and the export checklist.

findings.title: Strength: language-model endpoint handling matches ADR 12 closely
findings.evidence: "Not used: text would leave this computer. 'deepseek-v4.1-flash:cloud' is an Ollama cloud model. Ollama forwards requests to ollama.com, even though the address is local." Advanced has separate opt-ins for trustLocalServer ("for servers casefile can't check") and allowRemote. "Model checked against its fingerprint" reflects NER pinning.
findings.recommendation: Keep it. Also design the "local, unconfirmed" state, since ADR 12 says that state exists precisely so the app does not imply safety.

findings.title: Strength: verification and the affidavit gate follow ADRs 8 and 9
findings.evidence: Chronology: an unknown `{{grandmother}}` is marked "can't verify", and the copy says "If it changes later, it goes back to 'to check'". Draft: adoption one paragraph at a time with two attestation checkboxes (ownKnowledge/ownWords), no bulk adopt, a rewrite meter against the 50% threshold, export disabled while Claude paragraphs remain, and "Exports download to your computer, never into the case folder."
findings.recommendation: Keep it. Consider using ADR 9's exact attestation sentence so the logged attestation matches what the user ticked.
